column5: Yes and no. Actually it's pretty technical.\nI'm your only Scribe, but there's also a Scribe-in-training.\nHis name is Fortaime, and he's prepared to take over if needed.
column6: 算是，也不算。其实这事挺专业的。\n我是你唯一的书记官，但也有一名见习书记官。\n他叫福泰姆，随时准备接手。

column5: It's a recent addition to the ranks, but it helps out a lot.\nWithout a Scribe, your abilities would be pretty useless.\nHaving someone fully trained means no one misses a beat.
column6: 这是最近才增设的职位，但帮了大忙。\n没有书记官，你的能力基本派不上用场。\n有个受过完整训练的人，才能保证万无一失。

column5: Imagine if you had this vision while I was gone.\nJust from that, I think you can gauge Fortaime's importance.\nHe's a nice guy too, but I'm sure he's long since fled.
column6: 你想想，要是我不在的时候你看到那种幻象。\n光凭这一点，你应该就能明白福泰姆有多重要。\n他人也很好，不过我敢说他早就逃走了。

column5: I'm sure you'll meet him when you get out of here.\nHe tends to knock on your door first thing in the morning.\nSo let's focus on the matter at hand, alright?
column6: 等你离开这里，肯定会见到他的。\n他总是一大早就来敲你的门。\n所以咱们还是先专注眼前的事，好吗？

column5: Since I was a little kid, actually.\nI was trained to be your Scribe from the moment I could speak.\nIt's a prestigious position, and I couldn't exactly say no.
column6: 其实从我小时候起就是了。\n我一学会说话，就开始接受成为你书记官的训练。\n这是个荣耀的职位，我也没法拒绝。

column5: Some of the other children were jealous.\nTheir parents too, which seemed really immature to me.\nApparently, there's some competition for the role.
column6: 别的孩子里有几个很嫉妒。\n他们的父母也是，在我看来实在太不成熟了。\n看来这个职位还挺有竞争。

column5: But the Elder chose me, and like it or not, here I am.\nI guess I'm just blessed that I actually {i}do{/i} like this arrangement.\nIn the end, the spirits really were looking down on me.
column6: 但长老选了我，不管愿不愿意，我都站在这儿了。\n我大概很幸运，因为我{i}确实{/i}喜欢这样的安排。\n到头来，灵体们真的很眷顾我。

column5: Even if being here right now is terrifying, I'm still happy.\nDoing my duty to save Valinorth, it's a dream come true.\nWe don't know if the other kids would've fit this role.
column6: 就算现在待在这里很可怕，我依然很高兴。\n履行拯救瓦利诺斯的职责，这是我梦寐以求的事。\n谁知道别的孩子能不能胜任这个角色呢。

column5: Well I guess the answer is both yes and no.\nBefore my parents passed on, they took care of the paperwork.\nUntil I came of age, I had no choice but to obey.
column6: 我想答案算是，也不算。\n在我父母去世前，他们就把手续都办好了。\n在我成年之前，我别无选择，只能服从。

column5: When I did come of age, however, I got to choose.\nLeave Valinorth and pursue my own dreams, or be your Scribe.\nI guess it's pretty obvious which one I chose, huh?
column6: 但等我成年后，我就有得选了。\n离开瓦利诺斯去追寻自己的梦想，或者当你的书记官。\n我选了哪个，应该很明显吧？

column5: So, while I was forced into the role, I chose to stick with it.\nAlthough, if this is any indication, we might have to leave Valinorth.\nIn that case, I'd get to be your scribe, {i}and{/i} travel the world.
column6: 所以，虽然我是被迫接下这个职位的，但我选择继续做下去。\n不过，要是眼前这事是个预兆，我们也许得离开瓦利诺斯。\n那样的话，我既能当你的书记官，{i}又{/i}能周游世界。

column5: Well, we can't stop this attack from happening.\nWe can only take precautions, and mitigate the damage.\nYour life is valuable, so we should move you elsewhere.
column6: 这个嘛，我们没法阻止这场袭击发生。\n只能提前防范，把损失降到最低。\n你的性命很宝贵，所以我们应该把你转移到别处。

column5: And wherever you go, I'm bound to follow.\nWe'd be the first duo to operate outside of Valinorth.\nNever thought we'd actually make history, but here we are.
column6: 不管你去哪儿，我都跟着。\n我们会是第一对在瓦利诺斯之外行动的组合。\n从没想过我们真能创造历史，可事实就是如此。

column5: Yeah, and same to you.\nLook at this vision. We're going to do great things.\nLet's get to the bottom of this, and save our village together!
column6: 是啊，你也一样。\n看看这个幻象。我们会成就一番伟业。\n让我们一起查清真相，拯救我们的村庄！

column5: Hmm...
No, there's not much here.\nBut I guess if we spread out, we stand a better chance.\nNot that there's too much ground to cover.
column6: 不，这里没什么东西。\n不过我想，要是我们分头找，机会会大一些。\n反正要搜的地方也不多。

column5: If I knew, we'd have found it already.\nValessa seems to think Mylus left something behind.\nBut he isn't dumb. He wouldn't leave stuff out in the open.
column6: 我要是知道，早找到了。\n瓦莱莎似乎觉得迈勒斯留下了什么。\n可他又不傻，不会把东西明摆着放。

column5: If it were up to me, we'd all be long gone.\nI can't fight your choice though, it's your village.\nLet's do our best to hurry and get out of here.
column6: 要是我说了算，我们早该走远了。\n不过我没法反对你的选择，这是你的村子。\n咱们尽量快点，赶紧离开这里。

column5: Actually, I was going to ask you.\nI thought you two were in sync or something.\nDon't think I didn't notice your secret \"talks\".
column6: 其实我正想问你呢。\n我还以为你们俩心有灵犀什么的。\n别以为我没注意到你们那些秘密的“交谈”。

column5: But I'm not mad or anything.\nI know the relationship between you, and your culture.\nWhatever it is, it's not like you're plotting against me.
column6: 但我没生气，真的。\n我懂你们之间的关系，还有你们的文化。\n不管是什么，反正你们也不是在密谋对付我。

column5: Huh? You mean today, or in general?
column6: 啊？你是说今天，还是一直如此？

column5: Oh, I'm a mercenary from Mazeo.\nI was actually hired to come bring you back there.\nA summit is happening, and they want your input.
column6: 哦，我是从马泽奥来的佣兵。\n其实我是被雇来带你回去的。\n那边要开一场峰会，他们想听听你的意见。

column5: It's basically the hub of Alestia.\nPorts from there go to the rest of the known world.\nA huge city of commerce, it's full of strange people.
column6: 那里基本就是阿莱斯蒂亚的中心。\n从那儿出发的港口通往已知世界的各处。\n一座巨大的商业都市，到处都是奇怪的人。

column5: But you'd get stabbed in the back before you find help.\nThat's what puts people like me in business. Protectors of the weak.\nWell, not that I'm calling you weak, but you get the idea.
column6: 但你还没找到帮手，就先被人从背后捅刀了。\n这就是我们这行的生意所在。弱者的保护者。\n呃，我不是说你们弱，你懂我的意思就行。

column5: Because of its central location, it's the perfect meeting spot.\nThe Generals from Alarinthia and Balteus sail over annually.\nValinorth is non-partisan, so you usually sit this one out.
column6: 因为它地处中心，是绝佳的会面地点。\n阿拉林西亚和巴尔泰乌斯的将军们每年都会乘船过来。\n瓦利诺斯保持中立，所以通常不参与这种会议。

column5: Maybe it's a chance to get Valinorth more invested in Alestian politics.\nBut they want your input, and I've been sent to pick you up.\nI guess it's a good thing I got here when I did, right?
column6: 也许这是个让瓦利诺斯更深入参与阿莱斯蒂亚政局的机会。\n但他们想听你的意见，所以派我来接你。\n我及时赶到这里，算是件好事吧？

column5: Look, I don't ask for specifics.\nI do this to get paid, and make a living.\nIf you want, feel free to ask them when we get there.
column6: 听着，我不问细节。\n我干这行是为了挣钱糊口。\n你要是想知道，等我们到了，尽管去问他们。

column5: That is, if you two even agree to follow me.\nBut right now, I can't let you die on my watch.\nWe'll discuss the rest once we're out of harm's way.
column6: 前提是你们俩愿意跟我走。\n但现在，我不能让你们在我眼皮底下送命。\n等我们脱离危险，再谈其余的事。

column5: Is that an accusation of some kind?\nWhere I come from, you don't accuse the guy with a bigger sword.\nI'll pretend I didn't hear that, and carry on with this search.
column6: 这算是在指控我吗？\n在我的家乡，可没人会去指控一个剑比你大的人。\n我就当没听见，继续搜吧。

column5: Actually, I come from Alarinthia.\nPractically born with a blade in my hand.\nA figure of speech of course. Don't picture that.
column6: 其实我来自阿拉林西亚。\n几乎是握着刀剑出生的。\n当然，这是比喻。别去想象那画面。

column5: Eventually you grow up, and need money of your own.\nI took the first ship to Mazeo and started selling my sword arm.\nI don't miss that place at all. It's disgustingly warm and humid.
column6: 后来你长大了，得自己挣钱。\n我搭上第一班去马泽奥的船，开始当佣兵，靠这把剑吃饭。\n我一点都不想念那地方。又热又潮，让人受不了。

column5: Completely different than what you'd think.\nWe recognize power, not lineage, or claim to the throne.\nOr, I guess {i}they{/i} do, since I no longer live there.
column6: 跟你想象的完全不一样。\n我们看重的是力量，不是血统，也不是什么王位继承权。\n或者说，是{i}他们{/i}看重吧，毕竟我已经不住那儿了。

column5: Instead of elections, there's a tournament every few years.\nOnly the strongest tribe wins the right to rule Alarinthia.\nOf course, the rule is always contested shortly after.
column6: 没有选举，而是每隔几年办一场比武大会。\n只有最强的部落才能赢得统治阿拉林西亚的权利。\n当然，没过多久统治权总会被人挑战。

column5: It's good not to make any close friends.\nYou never know who you'll have to put to the blade.\nIt's a culture of war, and only the strongest prevail.
column6: 最好别交什么密友。\n你永远不知道哪天得对谁拔刀。\n那是个崇尚战争的文化，只有最强者才能胜出。

column5: You don't have to suck up to me. I know it's awful.\nThat's basically why I left the first chance I got.\nI'd take a stable living over that chaotic place.
column6: 你不用讨好我。我知道那儿很糟。\n所以我一有机会就离开了。\n比起那个混乱的地方，我更愿意过安稳日子。

column5: No offense, but you have it pretty easy here.\nThis is a paradise compared to what I had in Alarinthia.\nI mean, present circumstances excluded, of course.
column6: 别见怪，但你们这儿过得挺轻松的。\n跟我当年在阿拉林西亚的日子比，这里简直是天堂。\n当然，眼下的情况另当别论。

column5: The weak die out pretty fast, so not really.\nI'd say there's always a stable \"top ten\" list.\nIf someone isn't on it, they aren't worth your time.
column6: 弱者很快就淘汰了，所以也说不上。\n应该说总有一份稳定的“前十”名单。\n要是谁不在名单上，就不值得你花时间。

column5: Very funny. A joke question. I'll pass.
column6: 真好笑。这问题就是个玩笑。我跳过。

column5: Hey, we're talking about putting your life on the line.\nDo you really think you'd want protection from a nobody?
column6: 喂，我们说的是拿命去赌的事。\n你真觉得你会想要一个无名小卒来保护你吗？

column5: As you can tell, I'm very passionate about this.\nComes with the territory of being in the top ten.\nThough after this, I hope to rise a few ranks.
column6: 看得出来，我对这事很有热情。\n这是跻身前十的人必有的觉悟。\n不过经此一事，我希望能往上再升几名。

column5: Congratulations. You're now on my nerves.\nLet's change the subject before I leave you behind.
column6: 恭喜你。你现在让我心烦了。\n在我丢下你之前，咱们换个话题吧。

column5: No, I'm with my true family in Mazeo.\nWe have a different concept of family in Alarinthia.\nYou choose your family, and members come and go.
column6: 不，我真正意义上的家人都在马泽奥。\n在阿拉林西亚，我们对家人的概念不一样。\n家人是你自己选的，成员来来去去。

column5: When I left Alarinthia, I left that family behind.\nI made a new one in Mazeo, and they're no less important.\nWe don't go by blood in Alarinthia, but by choice.
column6: 我离开阿拉林西亚时，就把那个家抛在身后了。\n我在马泽奥组建了新的家庭，他们同样重要。\n在阿拉林西亚，我们不看血缘，只看选择。

column5: Yeah, and sorry if that sounds weird to you.\nThere's a big culture difference at play here.\nPerhaps you'll learn more when we leave Valinorth.
column6: 是啊，要是这话让你觉得奇怪，抱歉。\n这其中的文化差异很大。\n等我们离开瓦利诺斯，你或许会了解得更多。

column5: Not that I expect you to change your ways.\nBut it's always nice to learn about the world.\nAnyway, let's get back to the matter at hand.
column6: 我倒不是指望你改变自己的习惯。\n但多了解这个世界总是好事。\n总之，咱们还是回到正事上吧。

column5: They died during one of Alarinthia's tournaments.\nWhat stung worse, is that they made it to the final round.\nAlarinthia holds tournaments for the throne, not elections.
column6: 他们死在阿拉林西亚的某场比武大会上。\n更让人难受的是，他们一路打进了决赛。\n阿拉林西亚用比武大会来决定王位，而不是选举。

column5: But that's not why I left the nation at all.\nI heard about this in a letter a few years back.\nHaven't been home since, and don't plan on going either.
column6: 但那根本不是离开那个国家的原因。\n这是几年前我在一封信里得知的。\n从那以后我就没回过家，也不打算回去。

column5: Alarinthia is quite far away.\nIt easily takes a few days to reach by sea.\nThe climate is so different, I almost can't explain it.
column6: 阿拉林西亚相当远。\n坐船过去轻轻松松就得花上几天。\n那儿的气候差得太远，我几乎没法形容。

column5: Just, don't dress in layers.\nWear as little clothing as possible.\nYou're liable to melt into a puddle.
column6: 总之，别穿那么多层。\n衣服能少穿就少穿。\n不然你非得热化成一滩水不可。

column5: Alarinthia is known for its cutthroat political landscape.\nEven then, extreme heat is the leading cause of death.\nI'm not joking. Go unprepared and you'll pay for it.
column6: 阿拉林西亚以残酷的政治斗争闻名。\n即便如此，极端的酷热才是头号死因。\n我没开玩笑。毫无准备地过去，你会付出代价的。

column5: It's better to know beforehand, than go and regret it.\nWho knows where the path ahead might take you.\nJust doing my duty to help keep you safe.
column6: 事先了解总比去了再后悔强。\n谁知道前面的路会把你带向何方。\n我不过是尽本分，帮你保平安罢了。

column5: Well, yeah, if The Triumvirate {i}is{/i} truly responsible.\nAlestia is divided into four nations, right?\nValinorth, Mazeo, Alarinthia, and Balteus.
column6: 嗯，如果{i}确实{/i}是三人执政团干的。\n阿莱斯蒂亚分成四个国家，对吧？\n瓦利诺斯、马泽奥、阿拉林西亚，还有巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: Each nation has a General that serves The Triumvirate.\nThey rule in their stead, and make sure everything runs smoothly.\nExcept — you guessed it. The Elder, or General, of Valinorth.
column6: 每个国家都有一位效忠三人执政团的将军。\n他们代其掌权，确保一切运转顺畅。\n唯独——你猜到了。瓦利诺斯的长老，或者说将军。

column5: No one really knows why you remained untouched for so long.\nBut the theory is that they don't want to anger the spirits.\nYou know, because of all that spiritual energy residing here.
column6: 没人真正知道你们为什么这么久都没被染指。\n但有个说法是，他们不想激怒灵体。\n你懂的，因为这里盘踞着那么多灵力。

column5: So I'm thinking this is a power play.\nTake the fourth nation, and control the whole world.\nThey did the same thing to Mazeo about twenty years ago.
column6: 所以我猜这是一场权力博弈。\n拿下第四个国家，就能控制整个世界。\n大约二十年前，他们对马泽奥也是这么干的。

column5: The same thing that's happening here, but with less fire.\nThey occupied the free town, and placed a General in charge.\nThey used terrible force, but the town improved because of it.
column6: 跟这里发生的一样，只是没放那么多火。\n他们占领了那座自由城，派了个将军来管。\n他们动用了可怕的手段，但那座城也因祸得福。

column5: I'll never agree with their methods, but Mazeo is peaceful.\nIf they're burning villages down now, though? Unforgivable.\nPerhaps The Rebellion isn't in the wrong, after all.
column6: 我永远不会认同他们的手段，但马泽奥确实太平。\n可要是他们现在开始烧村子了？不可饶恕。\n或许反抗军并没有错。

column5: The way it looks right now? They already do.\nThat's why we need to get out of here as soon as possible.\nA stiff drink at Peregrino is sounding pretty good right now.
column6: 看眼下这情形？他们早就动手了。\n所以我们必须尽快离开这里。\n现在去佩雷格里诺喝上一杯烈酒，想想就很不错。

column5: Let's hurry up and get this finished.\nIt's turned into a fool's errand, and I'm no fool.
column6: 咱们快点把这事了结吧。\n这已经变成了白费力气，可我不是傻子。

column5: It's not like anything I've seen before.\nSo in tune with the spirits, you let them govern you.\nThe rest of Alestia has history in their own hands.
column6: 这跟我以前见过的东西都不一样。\n你们与灵体如此契合，任由它们来治理。\n阿莱斯蒂亚其他地方的历史都握在自己手里。

column5: Not that it's a bad thing, of course.\nIt's just different from the rest of the world.\nFrom what I've seen, the spirits have a good grasp on things.
column6: 当然，这倒不是什么坏事。\n只是跟世界其他地方不一样罢了。\n就我看到的而言，灵体把事情掌握得很好。

column5: Well, you're in the middle of a forest out here.\nYou know what they say about nature and spiritual energy.\nThe rest of the world has been deforested and settled differently.
column6: 这个嘛，你们这里地处森林之中。\n你也知道人们怎么说自然和灵力的关系。\n世界其他地方森林都砍光了，定居方式也不一样。

column5: It's not that they don't care for spirits.\nActually, it's more like they don't know anything else.\nThey've lived their entire lives in areas devoid of spiritual energy.
column6: 并不是说他们不在乎灵体。\n其实更像是他们压根不知道还有别的活法。\n他们一辈子都生活在没有灵力的地方。

column5: But Valinorth is so peaceful, while the rest of the world isn't.\nIt might very well be the influence of the spirit realm.\nYou have a good thing going here. I can't stand what's happening.
column6: 可瓦利诺斯这么安宁，世界其他地方却不然。\n这很可能就是灵界的影响。\n你们这里原本挺好。我实在看不下去正在发生的事。

column5: Well, let's not jump to conclusions.\nI'm a sellsword, there's no business in peace for me.\nAfter I retire though, it's always an option.
column6: 这个嘛，别急着下结论。\n我是佣兵，太平年月可没我这行的生意。\n不过等我退役了，这也不失为一条出路。

column5: If I live long enough to retire, that is.\nMy business isn't exactly the safest in the world.\nWhat's going on here is pretty good proof of that.
column6: 前提是我能活到退休。\n我这行可算不上世上最安全的。\n这里发生的事就是很好的证明。

column5: I push aside a few things, looking for anything of note.{w}\nIt's so cluttered that it's hard to find anything at all.{w}\nUlric slams his hand on the table, startling me.
column6: 我拨开几样东西，寻找任何值得注意的线索。{w}\n这里乱得根本什么都找不着。{w}\n乌尔里克一巴掌拍在桌上，吓了我一跳。

column5: This is my spot.\nFind somewhere else to look, alright?\nWe need to cover more ground if we want anything.
column6: 这是我的地盘。\n去别的地方找，行吗？\n想有收获，我们得搜更大的范围。

column5: He seems awfully defensive.{w}\nI notice he keeps looking at the papers.{w}\nAlmost like he knew what he wanted to find.
column6: 他好像戒备得很。{w}\n我注意到他老是盯着那些文件看。{w}\n简直就像他知道自己要找什么。

column5: It's a map of known Alestia, I've seen it many times.{w}\nWe're in Valinorth, with Mazeo to the North.{w}\nEast of Mazeo is Alarinthia, and North is Balteus.
column6: 这是已知阿莱斯蒂亚的地图，我见过很多次了。{w}\n我们在瓦利诺斯，北边是马泽奥。{w}\n马泽奥以东是阿拉林西亚，北边是巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: These four nations make up our world.{w}\nEach is governed over by a General of The Triumvirate.{w}\nExcept for Valinorth, which has remained non-partisan.
column6: 这四个国家构成了我们的世界。{w}\n每个都由三人执政团的一位将军治理。{w}\n只有瓦利诺斯例外，一直保持中立。

column5: It's odd how I remember the basics, but little else.{w}\nI wonder if this attack is an attempt to occupy Valinorth.{w}\nAfter that, all four nations would be under their control.
column6: 奇怪的是，我只记得这些基本的东西，其余的很少。{w}\n不知道这场袭击是不是想占领瓦利诺斯。{w}\n那样一来，四个国家就全在他们的掌控之下了。

column5: The flames haven't reached us yet.{w}\nMylus' house is much higher than the rest of Valinorth.{w}\nWe should hurry though, because it wouldn't be safe forever.
column6: 火焰还没烧到我们这儿。{w}\n迈勒斯的房子比瓦利诺斯其他地方高得多。{w}\n不过我们还是得快点，这里不可能一直安全。

column5: This isn't the time for sightseeing, you know.\nWe need to find information before we run out of time!
column6: 现在可不是观光的时候，你知道吧。\n我们得赶在时间耗尽前找到情报！

column5: Oh, sorry, I didn't think of that.\nKeeping watch is a good idea, actually.\nWhat do you see? Is it still safe out there?
column6: 哦，抱歉，我没考虑到这点。\n其实，有人放哨是个好主意。\n你看到什么了？外面还安全吗？

column5: No need to apologize, I'm just saying.\nBesides, at least you know it's still safe.\nKeeping watch isn't too bad of an idea, normally.
column6: 不用道歉，我随口说说而已。\n再说，至少你知道外面还安全。\n平时的话，放哨倒也不算个坏主意。

column5: I nod, and turn back to what I was doing.{w}\nMight want to look outside every few minutes.{w}\nThe last thing we need is an ambush.
column6: 我点点头，转回去继续手头的事。{w}\n也许该每隔几分钟往外看一次。{w}\n我们最不需要的就是中埋伏。

column5: I walk over to Valessa, and stand beside her.{w}\nShe's hard at work, reading papers and pushing books aside.{w}\nI've never seen someone quite so determined.
column6: 我走到瓦莱莎身边，站在她旁边。{w}\n她正埋头苦干，读着文件，把书往旁边推。{w}\n我从没见过这么坚定的人。

column5: Hey, have any luck yet?
column6: 嘿，有收获吗？

column5: Same, it's getting a bit discouraging.\nI'm thinking it would be something written.\nHave you checked all the tables and bookshelves?
column6: 一样，真有点让人泄气。\n我觉得应该是写成文字的东西。\n桌子书架你都查过了吗？

column5: Oh, uh, alright.\nBut maybe you should look as well.\nCheck out the tables and bookshelves?
column6: 哦，呃，好吧。\n不过你也许也该找找。\n去查查桌子和书架？

column5: I nod, and turn back to the rest of the room.{w}\nI guess I should help out, instead of watching them.{w}\nShe was certain we'd find something, and I trusted her.
column6: 我点点头，转回房间的其他地方。{w}\n我想我该帮把手，而不是光看着他们。{w}\n她确信我们会找到东西，我也信她。

column5: Hey, it's a ladder!
column6: 嘿，是架梯子！

column5: Actually, it's a \"step\"-ladder!
column6: 其实，它是一架“人”字梯！

column5: I doubt we have time to argue this.{w}\nTo avoid further conflict, I nod and move on.
column6: 我怀疑我们没时间争论这个。{w}\n为避免再生争执，我点点头走开了。

column5: I crawl under the table, it's full of useless trinkets.{w}\nWhatever we were looking for, I doubt it's down here.
column6: 我爬到桌子底下，满是没用的零碎玩意儿。{w}\n不管我们在找什么，我怀疑它不在下面。

column5: Hey, it isn't play time.\nGet out from under there.
column6: 喂，现在可不是玩的时候。\n从底下出来。

column5: I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that.\nIf you pass for authority around here, we're all dead.
column6: 我就当没听见。\n要是你这样子也算这里的权威，那我们全完了。

column5: Good, and don't let it happen again.\nWe can't afford to waste any time right now.
column6: 很好，别再犯了。\n我们现在可一点时间都耽误不起。

column5: I get out from under the table, after Ulric's verbal lashing.{w}\nHe might've disagreed, but we had to search everywhere we could.
column6: 在挨了乌尔里克一顿训之后，我从桌子底下钻了出来。{w}\n他也许不赞同，但我们得把所有能搜的地方都搜一遍。

column5: I have no idea what this pot is doing on the floor.{w}\nMylus may have been a good leader, but he's not organized.
column6: 我完全不知道这口锅怎么会摆在地上。{w}\n迈勒斯也许是个好领袖，但他做事没条理。

column5: He probably just left everything in a hurry.\nThe mess means he was looking for something, right?\nMaybe it was something to leave behind for us.
column6: 他大概只是匆匆忙忙就走了。\n这么乱，说明他当时在找东西，对吧？\n也许是特意留下来给我们的东西。

column5: This is it. This is what we needed!{w}\nI call over Ulric and Valessa, showing them what I found.{w}\nUlric seems tensed up, and even a little anxious.
column6: 就是这个。这正是我们需要的东西！{w}\n我把乌尔里克和瓦莱莎叫过来，给他们看我找到的东西。{w}\n乌尔里克似乎紧绷着，甚至有点紧张。

column5: So Mylus {i}was{/i} working with The Rebellion!\nApparently, he was sheltering a blade...?\nCould that be why they attacked us?
column6: 所以迈勒斯{i}确实{/i}在跟反抗军合作！\n据说，他窝藏了一把刀……？\n他们袭击我们会不会就是因为这个？

column5: Doing all this for a blade?\nLet's be realistic, Valessa.
column6: 搞这么大动静就为一把刀？\n现实点吧，瓦莱莎。

column5: It must've been very important.\nI'm assuming Mylus took it with him.\nI don't see any blades lying around here.
column6: 那一定非常重要。\n我猜迈勒斯把它带走了。\n我没看到这里有刀放着。

column5: But about this envoy he mentioned...?\nAnd this supposed \"special person\"?\nUlric, why did you lie to us?
column6: 可他提到的那个使者呢……？\n还有那个所谓的“特殊人物”？\n乌尔里克，你为什么要骗我们？

column5: It's true. Anybody would've figured it out by now.{w}\nHe seems to admit defeat and closes his eyes.{w}\nAlmost like he didn't want to see us as he spoke.
column6: 这是真的。到现在谁都能看出来了。{w}\n他似乎认了输，闭上了眼睛。{w}\n简直像说话时不愿看我们。

column5: We didn't think you'd come if you knew.\nI tried to hide it, but I guess there's no point anymore.\nAfter seeing this attack — I need to request your help.
column6: 我们觉得你要是知道了就不会来。\n我本想瞒着，但到现在也没意义了。\n看到这场袭击之后——我需要请求你们帮忙。

column5: This is far from the first village they'll raze.\nThey're up to something much bigger.\nThat's why you wanted to come here, right?
column6: 这远不是他们要夷平的第一座村庄。\n他们在谋划更大的事。\n所以你才想来这里，对吧？

column5: Yeah, you're right.\nThere's little time to argue, and nowhere else to go.\nIt looks like you got what you needed, Ulric.
column6: 是啊，你说得对。\n没时间争吵了，也没别的地方可去。\n看来你得偿所愿了，乌尔里克。

column5: Let's head back to The Grand Tree.\nThere might still be time.
column6: 我们回巨树去吧。\n也许还来得及。

column5: We all nod, acknowledging an unspoken truth.{w}\nUlric didn't care about those in The Grand Tree.{w}\nHe only knew that coming here would blow his cover.
column6: 我们都点了点头，默认了一个没有说出口的事实。{w}\n乌尔里克并不在乎巨树里的人。{w}\n他只知道，来这里会暴露他的身份。

column5: But I know that this information would be a huge advantage.{w}\nWe had a probable cause for their attack, {i}and{/i} knew Mylus' secret.{w}\nWe head back to the town square, instilled with hope.
column6: 但我知道，这个情报会是巨大的优势。{w}\n我们找到了他们袭击的可能原因，{i}还{/i}知道了迈勒斯的秘密。{w}\n我们满怀希望，朝镇上的广场走回去。

column5: The flames have spread, but it's not too bad.{w}\nI need to make sure I don't inhale too much smoke.{w}\nAs we take slow, cautious steps, my mind is conflicted.
column6: 火势蔓延了，但还不算太糟。{w}\n我得小心别吸进太多烟。{w}\n我们小心翼翼地缓步前行，我心里矛盾不已。

column5: There's one thing I can't seem to get off my mind.{w}\nThis blade, or whatever; was it worth all this?{w}\nDestroying an entire culture over something so simple?
column6: 有件事我怎么也放不下。{w}\n这把刀，或者说别的什么；真值得这一切吗？{w}\n为了这么个东西就毁掉一整个文明？

column5: Sorry, I can't see all that well.\nYou two will have to lead the way.\nI'm not as familiar with the surroundings.
column6: 抱歉，我看不太清楚。\n你们俩得带路了。\n我对这周围不太熟。

column5: We crouch, and make our way through Valinorth.{w}\nI have a rising urge to cough, but I try and hold it back.{w}\nWe wouldn't want to make it this far and get caught.
column6: 我们蹲着身子，穿过瓦利诺斯。{w}\n我越来越想咳嗽，但硬是忍住了。{w}\n可不想走了这么远还被逮住。

column5: The water tank is cracking and leaking its contents.{w}\nA small stream trickles down through the village.{w}\nThis would be our best tool to hinder the flames.
column6: 水箱裂了，水正往外漏。{w}\n一股细流顺着村子淌下去。{w}\n这会是我们阻挡火焰的最好工具。

column5: This isn't right, not at all.\nWhere is everyone, Ulric?\nThere's not a single body.
column6: 这不对劲，太不对劲了。\n人都去哪儿了，乌尔里克？\n一具尸体都没有。

column5: Like I said, they probably fled to safety.\nWe need to do that too, and fast.\nThere's nothing left for us here in Valinorth.
column6: 我说过了，他们大概是逃到安全的地方了。\n我们也得这么做，而且要快。\n瓦利诺斯已经没什么可留恋的了。

column5: Like I said, they could be at The Grand Tree.\nIt's isolated, and far away from here.\nI'm willing to bet the flames won't reach it.
column6: 我说过了，他们可能在巨树那里。\n那地方偏僻，离这里又远。\n我敢打赌火焰烧不到那儿。

column5: It doesn't make any sense, though.\nThink about it for a second.\nIn that alcove, we heard screams.
column6: 可这说不通啊。\n你回想一下。\n在那个凹室那儿，我们听到了尖叫声。

column5: The people of Valinorth were dying.\nNot only burning, but getting attacked.\nThere should be bodies all over the place.
column6: 瓦利诺斯的人在死去。\n不只是被烧，还遭到了攻击。\n尸体应该到处都是才对。

column5: She was right, and it bothered me as well.{w}\nThe current scene didn't match what we heard.{w}\nWas it possible for visions to warp this way?
column6: 她说得对，这也让我不安。{w}\n眼前的景象跟我们听到的对不上。{w}\n幻象有可能这样扭曲吗？

column5: What are you suggesting, Valessa?\nDo you think they {i}stole{/i} the bodies?
column6: 你想说什么，瓦莱莎？\n你觉得是他们把尸体{i}偷走{/i}了？

column5: If they did, there'd be blood.\nThere's nothing, not even a trace.\nIt doesn't make any sense, Ulric.
column6: 要真是那样，会有血迹。\n什么都没有，连一点痕迹都没留下。\n这根本说不通，乌尔里克。

column5: We have protocols for this kind of emergency.\nThere should've been people in The Grand Tree.\nEven if it was those too stubborn to shun tradition.
column6: 这种紧急情况我们有应对规程。\n巨树那儿本该有人的。\n哪怕只剩那些固执得不肯抛弃传统的人。

column5: Why is it so important, Valessa?\nYou seem to think everybody disappeared.\nWe should go to Peregrino, there {i}must{/i} be survivors.
column6: 这有什么要紧的，瓦莱莎？\n你好像觉得所有人都消失了。\n我们该去佩雷格里诺，那里{i}肯定{/i}有幸存者。

column5: I doubt we'll find answers in Valinorth.\nWe're on the right track, so let's not waste time.\nWe can reach Peregrino in a couple hours.
column6: 我觉得在瓦利诺斯找不到答案。\n我们方向没错，别浪费时间了。\n几个小时就能到佩雷格里诺。

column5: It made sense, and finally our goals aligned.{w}\nSearching for information, {i}and{/i} getting to safety.{w}\nSurvivors could be our biggest source of information.
column6: 这有道理，我们的目标终于一致了。{w}\n既能搜集情报，{i}又{/i}能去安全的地方。{w}\n幸存者可能是我们最大的情报来源。

column5: Besides, I'm sure that Mylus will be there.\nHe can tell you everything, Valessa.\nI'm sure he knows what's going on.
column6: 再说，我敢肯定迈勒斯会在那儿。\n他能把一切都告诉你，瓦莱莎。\n他肯定知道发生了什么。

column5: Let's say you're right, for arguments sake.\nWhy is it more important than going to The Grand Tree?\nTalking about it only seems to be wasting time.
column6: 就算你说得对，姑且这么假设。\n这为什么比去巨树更重要？\n光在这儿说，好像只是浪费时间。

column5: There might not {i}be{/i} anybody at The Grand Tree!\nI don't think we know what we're up against.\nWe should cut our losses and run, Ulric.
column6: 巨树那儿可能{i}根本{/i}没人！\n我觉得我们根本不清楚面对的是什么。\n我们该及时止损，赶紧跑，乌尔里克。

column5: You need to make up your mind, Valessa!\nRunning back and forth will get us all killed.\nAre we going to The Grand Tree or not?
column6: 你得拿定主意，瓦莱莎！\n这样来回跑会把我们都害死的。\n到底去不去巨树？

column5: It's true, she was changing her mind far too fast.{w}\nAt the moment, she seems to value our survival.{w}\nCould she be starting to doubt that this is a vision?
column6: 确实，她改主意改得太快了。{w}\n此刻，她好像更看重我们的安危。{w}\n她是不是开始怀疑这不过是一场幻象了？

column5: All I had to go on was her word.{w}\nI only believed her because it made sense at the time.{w}\nHow could I gather information if we leave Valinorth?
column6: 我唯一的依据就是她的话。{w}\n我之所以信她，只是因为这在那时说得通。{w}\n要是我们离开瓦利诺斯，我还怎么搜集情报？

column5: If you want to leave, we're going to Peregrino.\nIt'd be the first place for survivors to flee.\nIf Mylus is there, he can tell us all about this attack.
column6: 你要是想走，我们就去佩雷格里诺。\n那会是幸存者最先逃去的地方。\n迈勒斯要是在那儿，他能把这场袭击的来龙去脉都告诉我们。

column5: It's a good enough plan of action, and we nod to one another.{w}\nBut as we continue to move, everything changes.
column6: 这计划还算不错，我们相互点了点头。{w}\n可就在我们继续前行时，一切都变了。

column5: A laugh from atop the water tank. Almost maniacal.
column6: 水箱顶上传来一阵笑声。近乎癫狂。

column5: Such loyalty to the man who condemned you all.\nIf you want to know where Mylus is, I'd love to show you.\nI can even reunite you with the rest of the villagers.
column6: 对那个把你们全都定了罪的人，还真是忠心啊。\n你们想知道迈勒斯在哪儿的话，我很乐意带你们去。\n我甚至能让你们和其余的村民团聚。

column5: We stop in our tracks and look up at the water tank.{w}\nA silhouette of a man stands there, gripping a large blade.{w}\nIt's white and gold, with majesty embellished by the flames.
column6: 我们停下脚步，抬头望向水箱。{w}\n一个男人的剪影立在那里，握着一把大刀。{w}\n刀身金白相间，火焰更衬出它的威严。

column5: It reminds me of the suits of armor we fought earlier.{w}\nI have no doubt that there was some sort of relation.{w}\nWe must be looking at the man responsible for this.
column6: 它让我想起我们先前打过的那些铠甲。{w}\n我毫不怀疑两者之间有什么关联。{w}\n我们眼前这个人，肯定就是罪魁祸首。

column5: He jumps down from the water tank and lands with a roll.{w}\nI take a few steps back, ensuring that Ulric remains in the front.{w}\nIf his job was our protection, now was the time to shine through.
column6: 他从水箱上跳下来，就地一翻滚落地。{w}\n我后退几步，确保乌尔里克留在前面。{w}\n既然他的职责是保护我们，现在就该大显身手了。

column5: What a pitiful little village.\nIt's no fun when they don't put up a fight.\nDid you know what they did in their final moments?
column6: 多么可悲的小村庄啊。\n他们不反抗，就一点意思都没有。\n你知道他们最后一刻做了什么吗？

column5: They called out to you, Seer.\nThey wanted your help, and you let them down.\nI guess the stories I heard about you were wrong.
column6: 他们呼喊着你的名字，先知。\n他们盼着你来救，你却辜负了他们。\n看来我听说的关于你的传闻都是假的。

column5: They called out to you, Seeress.\nThey wanted your help, and you let them down.\nI guess the stories I heard about you were wrong.
column6: 他们呼喊着你的名字，先知。\n他们盼着你来救，你却辜负了他们。\n看来我听说的关于你的传闻都是假的。

column5: Sovy, you already have the blade.\nLet us leave, we can resolve this peacefully.
column6: 索维，你已经拿到那把刀了。\n放我们走，我们可以和平解决。

column5: No survivors, don't you remember the rule?\nLike a garden, we have to pluck all the weeds.
column6: 不留活口，你不记得规矩了吗？\n就像打理花园，杂草要连根拔净。

column5: Is that all these people are to you!?\nSovy, they have a culture, and history!
column6: 这些人对你来说就只是这样吗！？\n索维，他们有自己的文化，还有历史！

column5: Yes, but it's not {i}theirs{/i} that I'm interested in.\nIn fact, I'm only here to claim the Seer's soul.\nEverything else was just for fun. For sport.
column6: 是啊，但我感兴趣的可不是{i}他们的{/i}东西。\n其实，我来这里只是为了取走先知的灵魂。\n其余的不过是图个乐子，寻个刺激。

column5: Yes, but it's not {i}theirs{/i} that I'm interested in.\nIn fact, I'm only here to claim the Seeress' soul.\nEverything else was just for fun. For sport.
column6: 是啊，但我感兴趣的可不是{i}他们的{/i}东西。\n其实，我来这里只是为了取走先知的灵魂。\n其余的不过是图个乐子，寻个刺激。

column5: This becomes personal, as they seem to know each other.{w}\nThey both worked for opposing forces, I'm sure they've fought before.{w}\nIt sickens me that he likens killing the villagers to a sport.
column6: 事情变得私人了，他们俩好像认识。{w}\n他们各自为对立的势力效力，肯定交过手。{w}\n他竟把屠杀村民比作运动，真让我恶心。

column5: You don't mean...
column6: 你不会是说……

column5: My orders had nothing to do with burning down this village.\nI wasn't supposed to kill anyone unless I had to, either.\nBut you know, my Apprentice isn't very fun to train with.
column6: 我的命令跟烧掉这个村子毫无关系。\n除非迫不得已，我也不该杀人。\n可你知道，跟我的学徒对练实在没什么意思。

column5: Disgusting...\nValessa, take the Seer and run.\nI'll catch up with you at Peregrino.
column6: 恶心……\n瓦莱莎，带上先知快跑。\n我在佩雷格里诺跟你们会合。

column5: Disgusting...\nValessa, take the Seeress and run.\nI'll catch up with you at Peregrino.
column6: 恶心……\n瓦莱莎，带上先知快跑。\n我在佩雷格里诺跟你们会合。

column5: Ulric pulls out his blade, and assumes a fighting stance.{w}\nSovy does the same, and their eyes meet in deadlock.{w}\nI look at Valessa, and we nod before starting to run.
column6: 乌尔里克拔出刀，摆出战斗姿势。{w}\n索维也照做，两人的目光僵持着交汇。{w}\n我看向瓦莱莎，我们点了点头，随即开始奔逃。

column5: Unfortunately, we don't make it very far.{w}\nWe hear Ulric scream, and turn back to look.{w}\nSovy smirks at us, his blade deep in Ulric's abdomen.
column6: 不幸的是，我们没跑出多远。{w}\n我们听到乌尔里克的惨叫，回头看去。{w}\n索维冲我们得意地一笑，他的刀已深深没入乌尔里克的腹部。

column5: Where do you think you're going, you two?\nIt would be rude to leave before I'm done with you.\nWatch — and you'll see why you can {i}never{/i} win.
column6: 你们俩，以为要去哪儿？\n我还没把你们解决掉就走，可太失礼了。\n看着——你就会明白你们{i}永远{/i}赢不了。

column5: With a grin on his face, he twists the blade inside Ulric.{w}\nDefying all possibility, the gear on the base starts to spin.{w}\nSoon after, everything is engulfed in a blinding white light.
column6: 他咧嘴一笑，在乌尔里克体内转动刀身。{w}\n不可思议的是，刀柄底部的齿轮开始转动。{w}\n紧接着，一切都被刺眼的白光吞没。

column5: Please, run...
column6: 快跑……

column5: We hear Ulric's final words as the light subsides.{w}\nWhen everything is back to normal, he's completely gone.{w}\nNo blood, no body, just Sovy standing there with pride.
column6: 光芒消退时，我们听到了乌尔里克最后的话。{w}\n等一切恢复如常，他已彻底消失。{w}\n没有血，没有尸体，只有索维得意地站在那里。

column5: What!?\nWhat did you do...!?
column6: 什么！？\n你做了什么……！？

column5: I put his spirit to good use.\nLike I plan to do with your little friend.
column6: 我让他的灵体发挥了用处。\n就像我打算对你这位小朋友做的事一样。

column5: He points behind us, and we turn to look.{w}\nThe scattered pieces of armor on the ground start to move.{w}\nThey assemble, forming bodies that move in a slow, stiff fashion.
column6: 他指向我们身后，我们转身看去。{w}\n地上散落的铠甲碎片动了起来。{w}\n它们拼合起来，组成动作迟缓僵硬的身躯。

column5: But after a few moments, the movements become more natural.{w}\nIt isn't much longer until an army of automatons blocks our path.{w}\nThere was nowhere to go. Sovy blocked the other side.
column6: 但过了片刻，动作变得自然起来。{w}\n没过多久，一支自动人偶组成的军队堵住了我们的去路。{w}\n无处可逃。索维封住了另一边。

column5: You — you're using their spirits to power that armor?\nDoes that mean we've been fighting our own...!?
column6: 你——你在用他们的灵体给那些铠甲供能？\n那我们一直在跟自己人打……！？

column5: Now you finally understand.\nThe force of life itself bends to The Triumvirate.\nThere's no way that you could hope to stop us.
column6: 你终于明白了。\n连生命之力都臣服于三人执政团。\n你们根本别想阻止我们。

column5: He takes slow steps toward me, holding out his blade.{w}\nI finally understood why it was so important to The Triumvirate.{w}\nThey could command an army of spirits simply by possessing it.
column6: 他握着刀，缓缓朝我走来。{w}\n我终于明白它为什么对三人执政团如此重要。{w}\n只要拥有它，他们就能号令一支灵体大军。

column5: As soon as I harvest the Seer's soul, I'll leave.\nValessa, if you behave, I might let you go.\nVisit The Rebels. Tell them what's coming.
column6: 等我收割了先知的灵魂，我就走。\n瓦莱莎，你要是乖乖听话，我也许会放你走。\n去反抗军那儿，告诉他们什么要来了。

column5: As soon as I harvest the Seeress' soul, I'll leave.\nValessa, if you behave, I might let you go.\nVisit The Rebels. Tell them what's coming.
column6: 等我收割了先知的灵魂，我就走。\n瓦莱莎，你要是乖乖听话，我也许会放你走。\n去反抗军那儿，告诉他们什么要来了。

column5: This is it. If he attacked me, the vision would end.{w}\nI was armed with all the information I needed to counter this attack.{w}\nThe true purpose, the major players, and even the nature of the blade.
column6: 就是现在。只要他攻击我，幻象就会结束。{w}\n我已经掌握了应对这场袭击所需的全部情报。{w}\n真正的目的、关键人物，甚至那把刀的本质。

column5: He was so certain of his victory, he had no idea.{w}\nI took a step forward, embracing what was to come.{w}\nWhen this future came for Valinorth, we would be ready.
column6: 他如此笃定自己会赢，浑然不知。{w}\n我向前迈出一步，坦然迎接即将到来的一切。{w}\n等这个未来降临瓦利诺斯时，我们会做好准备。

column5: He thrusts the blade inside of me with little effort.{w}\nThe pain is so intense, but I'm overcome with hope.{w}\nAs my vision fades, I find the strength to say one final thing.
column6: 他毫不费力地把刀刺入我体内。{w}\n剧痛难忍，可我心中却充满希望。{w}\n视野渐渐模糊，我攒起力气，说出最后一句话。

column5: Hmm...?
My eyes shoot open and I instinctively clutch my gut.{w}\nThe pain from the vision lingers, pulsing through my body.{w}\nPanting heavily, I squirm in pain, waiting for it to fade.
column6: 我猛地睁开眼，下意识地捂住腹部。{w}\n幻象中的疼痛还残留着，一阵阵传遍全身。{w}\n我大口喘着气，痛得扭动身体，等着它消退。

column5: I fall off the side of my bed, and slam into the floor.{w}\nThankfully, this makes me fully lucid, stopping the pain.{w}\nFor a moment, it's as if I existed in both scenarios.
column6: 我从床边摔了下来，重重砸在地上。{w}\n幸好这一摔让我彻底清醒，疼痛也止住了。{w}\n有那么一瞬间，我仿佛同时存在于两个场景之中。

column5: I rise to a sitting position, and focus on my breathing.{w}\nStill in shock at what happened, my heart beats frantically.{w}\nIt takes a while before it slows down, but I happily wait.
column6: 我坐起身，专注地调整呼吸。{w}\n我仍对发生的事惊魂未定，心脏狂跳不止。{w}\n过了好一会儿才慢下来，但我乐意等着。

column5: When these negative feelings subside, I stand up.{w}\nThe vision I just experienced plays on a loop in my head.{w}\nI had to warn Mylus, I had to ensure this didn't happen!
column6: 等这些负面情绪平息，我站了起来。{w}\n刚才经历的幻象在脑海里循环播放。{w}\n我必须警告迈勒斯，我必须阻止这一切发生！

column5: A knock sounds on my door, and I lock up in fright.{w}\nAfter what I just saw, my mind is filled with anxiety.{w}\nThankfully, as a voice calls out to me, I'm put at ease.
column6: 门上传来敲门声，我吓得浑身一僵。{w}\n刚看到那样的事，我心里满是焦虑。{w}\n幸好，一个声音朝我喊来，我才放宽了心。

column5: Hey Seer, open up!\nDon't make me wait all day again!
column6: 嘿，先知，开门！\n别又让我等一整天！

column5: Hey Seeress, open up!\nDon't make me wait all day again!
column6: 嘿，先知，开门！\n别又让我等一整天！

column5: It's Fortaime. He's my best friend, and Valessa's student.{w}\nAs my Scribe, she had to train a \"back-up\", so to speak.{w}\nA terrible scenario to plan for, but it had to be done.
column6: 是福泰姆。他是我最好的朋友，也是瓦莱莎的学生。{w}\n作为我的书记官，她得培养一个所谓的“替补”。{w}\n要为之做准备的设想很糟糕，但不得不做。

column5: I rush over to the door and quickly unlock it.{w}\nWelcoming him in, I notice a huge grin on his face.{w}\nI feel relaxed. It's a brief reminder of safety.
column6: 我冲到门口，迅速打开门锁。{w}\n把他迎进来时，我注意到他脸上挂着大大的笑容。{w}\n我放松下来。这短暂地提醒我，这里是安全的。

column5: Did you just wake up!?\nOh jeeze, I hope we won't be late.\nDon't tell me you forgot what day it is!
column6: 你该不会刚醒吧！？\n哎呀，可别迟到了。\n别告诉我你忘了今天是什么日子！

column5: Hey, I definitely took a bath!\nI just rushed it, because I had to pick you up.\nEnough about me, though. This is your special day!
column6: 喂，我可是洗过澡的！\n只是赶时间，因为得来接你。\n不过别光说我了。今天是你的大日子！

column5: Stop that! You're saying weird stuff again!\nI should be the one flattering you, it's {i}your{/i} day.\nSomething like this only happens once a generation.
column6: 别说了！你又在说些奇怪的话了！\n该奉承你的是我才对，今天可是{i}你{/i}的日子。\n这种事一代人才轮得到一次。

column5: Hey, I'm just trying to be nice!\nI didn't mean to steal your thunder.\nAfter all, this day is all about {i}you{/i}!
column6: 喂，我只是想表示好意嘛！\n我不是有意抢你风头的。\n毕竟，今天的主角就是{i}你{/i}！

column5: Huh? Did you forget?\nOh well, I don't blame you.\nThere's lots going on lately.
column6: 啊？你忘了？\n哎，我不怪你。\n最近事儿太多了。

column5: You're being officially inducted!\nYou know, the ceremony to brand you as a Seer?\nIt should've happened ages ago, but stuff got in the way.
column6: 你要正式受封了！\n就是那场给你烙上先知印记的仪式。\n早该办了，可总有事耽搁。

column5: You're being officially inducted today!\nYou know, the ceremony to brand you as a Seeress?\nIt should've happened ages ago, but stuff got in the way.
column6: 你要正式受封了！\n就是那场给你烙上先知印记的仪式。\n早该办了，可总有事耽搁。

column5: Let's not delay it anymore, alright?\nJust sign this paper before we go.\nMylus wants it. Consent for the ceremony.
column6: 咱们别再拖了，好吗？\n走之前把这份文件签了。\n迈勒斯要的，是仪式的同意书。

column5: Thanks, [firstname]!\nThis is exactly what he'll need.\nPut on something fancy, I'll wait outside.
column6: 谢啦，[firstname]！\n这正是他需要的。\n换身讲究点的衣服，我在外面等。

column5: I reach out to try and stop him, but he's already gone.{w}\nIt's for the better though, as he mustn't know what I saw.{w}\nThe only people authorized to know were Mylus and Valessa.
column6: 我伸手想拦住他，可他已经走了。{w}\n不过这样也好，他绝不能知道我看到了什么。{w}\n获准知情的人只有迈勒斯和瓦莱莎。

column5: I walk over to my wardrobe, to look for an outfit.{w}\nAs Fortaime pointed out, I'm still in my smallclothes.{w}\nIf it was a big day, I guess I'd have to dress the part.
column6: 我走到衣柜前，想找身衣服。{w}\n正如福泰姆指出的，我还穿着里衣。{w}\n既然是个大日子，我想我得穿得像样点。

column5: Yes, that should be a fine choice.{w}\nI slip into the menswear, and turn back to my room.{w}\nI take in everything at once. It's a huge mess.
column6: 好，这应该是个不错的选择。{w}\n我换上男装，转身回到房间。{w}\n我一眼扫过一切。乱得一塌糊涂。

column5: Yes, that should be a fine choice.{w}\nI slip into the dress, and turn back to my room.{w}\nI take in everything at once. It's a huge mess.
column6: 好，这应该是个不错的选择。{w}\n我换上裙子，转身回到房间。{w}\n我一眼扫过一切。乱得一塌糊涂。

column5: Once I meet Fortaime, we might be busy for a while.{w}\nI should finish up any last minute business while I can.{w}\nBut at the same time, I shouldn't keep him waiting for long.
column6: 一旦见到福泰姆，我们可能会忙上一阵。{w}\n我该趁现在把手头最后的琐事了结掉。{w}\n但与此同时，也不该让他等太久。

column5: The town looks so peaceful, and so quiet.{w}\nIt's a far cry from the way I saw it last night.{w}\nHopefully the vision was far off, and not impending.
column6: 小镇看起来如此安宁，如此寂静。{w}\n跟我昨晚看到的景象天差地别。{w}\n但愿那幻象离我们还远，而不是迫在眉睫。

column5: This sword has been above my bed for as long as I can remember.{w}\nIt's ceremonial, and it couldn't really do anything in a fight.{w}\nFortaime gave it to me when we were younger. That's how we met.
column6: 从我记事起，这把剑就一直挂在我床头上方。{w}\n它是仪式用的，真打起来派不上什么用场。{w}\n是福泰姆在我们小时候送给我的。我们就是这么认识的。

column5: I never water this plant anymore, but it's still alive.{w}\nAllegedly, plantlife is a container for spiritual energy.{w}\nIt's odd, because in that case, plants are immortal.
column6: 我已经不再给这株植物浇水了，可它还活着。{w}\n据说，植物是灵力的容器。{w}\n说来奇怪，照这么说，植物岂不是不死的。

column5: I was supposed to gather bags of grain for Mylus.{w}\nValinorth is self-sustaining, and we take turns harvesting.{w}\nBut I think I have something more important to talk to him about.
column6: 我本该去给迈勒斯收集几袋谷子的。{w}\n瓦利诺斯自给自足，大家轮流收割。{w}\n但我想，有更重要的事要跟他谈。

column5: My cooking space is so messy, it's embarrassing.{w}\nI'm glad Fortaime didn't stay and visit.{w}\nIt would've been lecture after lecture.
column6: 我的灶台乱得让人难为情。{w}\n幸好福泰姆没留下来串门。{w}\n不然又是一顿接一顿的唠叨。

column5: This carpet is pretty luxurious. Valessa gave it to me.{w}\nIt sure beats walking on the cold wooden floor.{w}\nScribes go all-out when it's their Seer's birthday.
column6: 这块地毯挺华贵的。是瓦莱莎送给我的。{w}\n总比踩在冰冷的地板上强多了。{w}\n每逢先知生日，书记官都会不惜血本。

column5: This carpet is pretty luxurious. Valessa gave it to me.{w}\nIt sure beats walking on the cold wooden floor.{w}\nScribes go all-out when it's their Seeress' birthday.
column6: 这块地毯挺华贵的。是瓦莱莎送给我的。{w}\n总比踩在冰冷的地板上强多了。{w}\n每逢先知生日，书记官都会不惜血本。

column5: This bread is as hard as a rock!{w}\nBut I guess it's better than nothing.{w}\nI'm in a hurry, I'll grab one to eat on the go.
column6: 这面包硬得像石头！{w}\n不过有总比没有强。{w}\n我赶时间，拿一个边走边吃吧。

column5: I hope that Fortaime never has to step up as Scribe.{w}\nHowever, at the moment, the future seems very uncertain.
column6: 我希望福泰姆永远不必接任书记官一职。{w}\n然而眼下，未来显得十分不确定。

column5: Last time Fortaime came over, he left his journal.{w}\nOf course, he has nothing to hide, and he's always open.{w}\nI often benefit from his writings. He's smarter than he lets on.
column6: 上次福泰姆来的时候，把他的日记落下了。{w}\n当然，他没什么可隐瞒的，一向坦诚。{w}\n我常从他的文字里获益。他比表面看起来聪明得多。

column5: It's actually kind of scary to think about.{w}\nThe spirits have more sway over us than we know.
column6: 仔细想想，其实有点吓人。{w}\n灵体对我们的影响，比我们知道的还要大。

column5: It's a book on the true reach of the spirits.{w}\nA very divisive topic, and one that's always debated.
column6: 这是一本讲灵体真正影响范围的书。{w}\n一个极具争议、总被拿来辩论的话题。

column5: This book makes me wonder, where did we come from?{w}\nIf The Triumvirate are righteous, why would they attack us?{w}\nAnd if they didn't create Alestia, then who did...?
column6: 这本书让我思考，我们从何而来？{w}\n如果三人执政团是正义的，为什么要袭击我们？{w}\n如果阿莱斯蒂亚不是他们创造的，那又是谁……？

column5: One of my books, on the creation of Alestia.{w}\nAlgus Veilleur is one of the most famous scholars in the world.{w}\nI tried to collect some of his works, but he wrote so much.
column6: 我的一本书，讲的是阿莱斯蒂亚的创世。{w}\n阿尔古斯·维勒是世上最著名的学者之一。{w}\n我本想收集他的一些著作，可他写得太多了。

column5: I really wish I could just hop back into bed.{w}\nBut I guess I have responsibilities and stuff.{w}\nI shouldn't keep Mylus in the dark for much longer.
column6: 我真希望能直接跳回床上。{w}\n可我想我还有责任在身之类的。{w}\n我不该再瞒着迈勒斯太久了。

column5: There isn't much use for my armoire right now.{w}\nI already grabbed the suit, and that's all I need.{w}\nBut maybe I'll organize it more when I get the chance.
column6: 现在我的衣柜没多大用处。{w}\n我已经拿了那套男装，这就够了。{w}\n不过有机会的话，也许我会把它再整理整理。

column5: There isn't much use for my armoire right now.{w}\nI already grabbed the dress, and that's all I need.{w}\nBut maybe I'll organize it more when I get the chance.
column6: 现在我的衣柜没多大用处。{w}\n我已经拿了那条裙子，这就够了。{w}\n不过有机会的话，也许我会把它再整理整理。

column5: The town looks so peaceful, and so quiet.{w}\nIt's a far cry from the way I saw it last night.{w}\nHopefully the vision was far off, and not impending.
column6: 小镇看起来如此安宁，如此寂静。{w}\n跟我昨晚看到的景象天差地别。{w}\n但愿那幻象离我们还远，而不是迫在眉睫。

column6: 你即将首次进入世界地图。{w}\n点击角落里的问号查看教程。{w}\n剧情流程和探索玩法会有更详细的说明。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Well, it's a huge mess, for one.\nYou should see mine. It's flawless.\nI'm actually tempted to start cleaning.
column6: 首先，这里乱得一塌糊涂。\n你该看看我的房间，一尘不染。\n我其实有点忍不住想开始打扫了。

column5: But I know I shouldn't do that without permission.\nLast time I did that, I got into a whole mess of trouble.\nStory for another time I guess. Or, whenever you ask.
column6: 但我知道，没得到允许不该这么做。\n上次我这么干，惹了一堆麻烦。\n这故事改天再讲吧。或者，你什么时候问都行。

column5: I'm pretty sure that's an understatement, [firstname]!\nI just can't {i}stand{/i} when something is out of place.\nIt drives me insane, makes me freak out.
column6: 我敢说这还说得太轻了，[firstname]！\n我{i}实在受不了{/i}东西不在它该在的位置。\n这让我抓狂，简直要发疯。

column5: Don't be offended if you see me messing around.\nEverything has an order, a perfect place it should be.\nI just like putting things where they belong!
column6: 要是看到我瞎收拾，别见怪。\n每样东西都有它的次序，有它该在的完美位置。\n我就是喜欢把东西归到该放的地方！

column5: Oh, thank goodness!\nI was so scared you'd get mad at me.\nGive me a few minutes, I won't take long.
column6: 哦，谢天谢地！\n我还怕你会生我的气呢。\n给我几分钟，不会太久。

column5: Wait, why is there a sack of grain on the floor?\nAnd your cooking area is an absolute mess!\nThis is going to take longer than I thought.
column6: 等等，地上怎么会有袋谷子？\n还有你的灶台，简直乱成一团！\n这比我想的要花更长时间。

column5: Is that a serious offer...?\nBecause you know, I'm very interested.\nEven if Mylus says that's against the rules.
column6: 这提议是认真的吗……？\n因为你知道，我非常感兴趣。\n就算迈勒斯说这违反规矩。

column5: But I'll wait until you make a formal offer.\nSometimes I act on impulse and make a fool of myself.\nThere was big trouble last time I cleaned without permission.
column6: 但我会等你正式提出来。\n有时我一冲动就出洋相。\n上次我没经允许就打扫，惹了大麻烦。

column5: I saw a house so dirty, I couldn't resist.\nIt turned out to be Mylus' spare study home.\nEverything was messed up, but with purpose.
column6: 我看到一栋房子脏得不成样，实在忍不住。\n结果那是迈勒斯备用的书房。\n一切都很乱，但乱得有讲究。

column5: He said it took him months to recover.\nI messed with his stuff and threw his studies off.\nI'll never forgive myself for doing that, [firstname].
column6: 他说花了好几个月才缓过来。\n我动了他的东西，把他的研究全打乱了。\n我永远不会原谅自己，[firstname]。

column5: He said it was \"unbecoming\" of me.\nI had to look up the word, but I guess it's true.\nAs a scribe-in-training, I need to show {i}some{/i} class.
column6: 他说我有失“体统”。\n那词我还得查字典，但我想他说得没错。\n身为见习书记官，我总得有点{i}风度{/i}。

column5: It's pretty great, actually.\nEverything is given to me by Valinorth.\nMoney, food, a house. You name it.
column6: 其实挺不错的。\n一切都是瓦利诺斯给我的。\n钱、食物、房子，应有尽有。

column5: I work with Valessa more than you, though.\nI'm kind of disappointed about that.\nWe tend to role-play real scenarios.
column6: 不过我跟瓦莱莎共事比跟你多。\n对此我有点失望。\n我们常常模拟真实的场景来演练。

column5: She'll take on your role, and I'll take on hers.\nPlaying a Scribe {i}for{/i} a Scribe. Best possible training.\nUnfortunately, I doubt I'll ever be a real one.
column6: 她扮演你的角色，我扮演她的。\n{i}演{/i}书记官的书记官。最好的训练方式。\n可惜，我恐怕永远成不了真正的书记官。

column5: I don't think there's any protocol for that.\nBut I assume Mylus has the final word there.\nOr whoever the Elder is at any given time.
column6: 我觉得这种事没有先例可循。\n但我想那得迈勒斯说了算。\n或者说，谁当长老就谁说了算。

column5: Sometimes you just have to go with the flow.\nBut I hope you're not trying to say Valessa is bad.\nIs there something I'm not seeing here...?
column6: 有时候你就得随波逐流。\n但希望你不是想说瓦莱莎不好。\n是不是有什么我没看出来的……？

column5: Whoa, are you serious?\nI got the feeling that I kind of annoyed you.\nSorry, I don't know how to respond to that!
column6: 哇，你是认真的吗？\n我还以为我有点惹你烦了呢。\n抱歉，我不知道该怎么回应这话！

column5: But I really don't think I can be your Scribe.\nI can only take over if something happens to Valessa.\nAnd trust me, I {i}really{/i} don't want that to happen.
column6: 但我真觉得我当不了你的书记官。\n只有当瓦莱莎出事，我才能接手。\n相信我，我{i}真的{/i}不希望那样的事发生。

column5: We'll have to find other ways to work together.\nOr we could even hang out in our off time.\nThere's no rule against doing that.
column6: 我们得另找办法一起做事。\n或者我们甚至可以休息时一起玩。\n又没有规矩禁止这么做。

column5: Whoa, do you have a thing for her?\nI guess it's natural. You work together a lot.\nNever would've expected it, that's all.
column6: 哇，你是不是对她有意思？\n我想这也正常。你们常在一起共事。\n只是我从没料到而已。

column5: Wait, don't answer that question!\nI can't have any gossip on the brain.\nWhatever you feel, keep it private!
column6: 等等，别回答这个问题！\n我脑子里可不能装八卦。\n不管你什么感觉，都藏在心里！

column5: Oh, I guess I jumped to conclusions again.\nI really need to stop doing stuff like that.\nI hope I was able to help your curiosity though.
column6: 哦，我猜我又妄下结论了。\n我真得改改这毛病。\n不过希望我满足了你的好奇心。

column5: We have to obey the rules set in stone by Valinorth.\nI'm just happy that we all get along with each other.\nThis trio could've been a lot worse, if you ask me.
column6: 我们得遵守瓦利诺斯定下的铁律。\n我挺高兴我们几个相处得不错。\n要我说，这三人组本可能糟得多。

column5: Well, I really love climbing trees.\nAside from that, I love reading, and cleaning.\nIt's a simple life here, but I have no problem with it.
column6: 这个嘛，我很喜欢爬树。\n除此之外，我喜欢读书，还有打扫。\n这里生活简单，但我一点不介意。

column5: I have a lot of time off. Way more than Valessa.\nHonestly, I think I only do half of what she does.\nJust means I need to keep myself occupied.
column6: 我空闲时间很多。比瓦莱莎多得多。\n老实说，我觉得我干的只有她的一半。\n这就意味着我得找事打发时间。

column5: If you see me with cuts and bruises, don't freak out.\nI'm pushing myself to the limits. Climbing bigger trees.\nBefore you know it, I'll be on top of The Grand Tree.
column6: 要是看到我浑身是伤，别惊慌。\n我在挑战自己的极限，爬更高的树。\n不知不觉，我就会登上巨树的顶端。

column5: Wait, seriously?\nThat sounds awesome, [firstname]!\nI'll have to choose something easy, then.
column6: 等等，真的吗？\n听起来太棒了，[firstname]！\n那我得挑点简单的才行。

column5: I don't want to throw you right into it.\nValinorth needs you, and I won't screw that up.\nBut it might be fun having an apprentice to teach.
column6: 我不想一上来就让你应付难事。\n瓦利诺斯需要你，我不能把这事搞砸。\n不过带个徒弟教教，也许挺有意思。

column5: Nope, just the perfect amount!\nIf you aren't pushing yourself, you aren't winning.\nThere's an exact formula to it, and I'm playing it safe.
column6: 不，是刚刚好的量！\n不逼自己一把，就赢不了。\n这其中有个精确的法则，我是在稳妥行事。

column5: About... five years less than Valessa.\nAfter The Triumvirate took over Mazeo, we were scared.\nSo I think I was a \"worst case scenario\" type of thing.
column6: 大概……比瓦莱莎少五年吧。\n三人执政团占领马泽奥之后，我们都吓坏了。\n所以我觉得我是那种“最坏情况下的备用方案”。

column5: Some people say that Mylus' Father trained him, too.\nThat's why he was able to take over so easily.\nThat means he's like me, but for the position of Elder.
column6: 有人说，迈勒斯的父亲也培养过他。\n所以他才这么容易就接了班。\n也就是说他跟我一样，只不过对应的是长老之位。

column5: You must be messing with me. Is this a test...?\nI'd rather not talk about that, if it's all the same.\nAt least approach the subject a little more casually.
column6: 你一定是在逗我。这是在试探我吗……？\n要是不介意的话，我还是不想谈这个。\n至少换个更随意点的方式提。

column5: Same, that would be awful!\nWe're definitely like a small family here.\nI couldn't live without either of you.
column6: 一样，那太可怕了！\n我们这儿真像一个小家庭。\n少了你们俩谁，我都活不下去。

column5: I feel weird, existing as a fail-safe.\nBut I'm free to do much more in my spare time.\nI love this position, and I'm glad to know both of you.
column6: 作为一道保险措施而存在，感觉怪怪的。\n但我的闲暇时间能自由做更多事。\n我喜欢这个职位，也很高兴认识你们俩。

column5: I don't think I'm really allowed to do that.\nThe training I go through is already mentally exhausting.\nI need to devote my spare time to blowing off steam.
column6: 我觉得我其实没被允许那么做。\n我接受的训练已经很耗心力了。\n我得把闲暇时间用来发泄解压。

column5: Of course, this is under Mylus' orders.\nI'm sure I could handle something if I really wanted.\nBut getting in trouble with him really isn't worth it.
column6: 当然，这是迈勒斯的命令。\n要是真想，我肯定也能应付点什么。\n但惹上他的麻烦实在不值当。

column5: To be honest, I just like helping people.\nSo probably cleaning up here and there, keeping tidy.\nI consider a day successful if I've made someone else smile.
column6: 老实说，我就是喜欢帮人。\n所以大概就是到处打扫打扫，保持整洁。\n只要能让别人露出笑容，我就觉得这一天没白过。

column5: Maybe I could be a problem solver or something.\nPeople always need some help, so I'd never go bored.\nIt would always involve something new and exciting.
column6: 也许我可以当个专门解决问题的人之类的。\n人总是需要帮忙，所以我永远不会觉得无聊。\n总能碰上新鲜又刺激的事。

column5: Of course, I'm getting ahead of myself here.\nMylus says I'm not allowed to do any extra work.\nTraining has to be my most important focus.
column6: 当然，我这是想得太远了。\n迈勒斯说我不准做任何额外的工作。\n训练必须是我最重要的重心。

column5: That sounds awesome, it really does.\nBut I'd never hear the end of it from Mylus.\nIf I overload my brain with work, I'll slip up.
column6: 听起来很棒，真的。\n可迈勒斯会没完没了地念叨我。\n要是用工作把脑子塞满，我就会出错。

column5: He says I always need to be \"at the ready\".\nUnfortunately, that leads to a lot of waiting around.\nWho would've thought too much spare time is an issue?
column6: 他说我必须随时“待命”。\n可惜这样一来，就常常只能干等着。\n谁会想到空闲太多也会成问题呢？

column5: That's why I do things I can always cut short.\nClimbing a tree? Just hop down, and try again later.\nCleaning? Just stop. The mess isn't going anywhere.
column6: 所以我都做些随时能中断的事。\n爬树？跳下来，回头再试就是了。\n打扫？停下就行。乱摊子又不会长腿跑掉。

column5: I could think of {i}much{/i} worse things to do.\nConsidering that, it's not too bad on my end.\nMy life is simple, and there's some beauty in that.
column6: 我能想到{i}远{/i}比这糟糕的事。\n这么一想，我这处境也不算太差。\n我的生活很简单，其中自有一种美。

column5: You and Valessa always seem so busy.\nI'd rather stay in my situation than be overworked.\nI'm sure you cope with it, but I doubt I could.
column6: 你和瓦莱莎看起来总是忙得不行。\n比起累死累活，我倒宁愿保持现状。\n你们肯定应付得来，但换了我可不行。

column5: I hope I never have to step up, either.\nThat would mean something terrible happened to Valessa.\nI don't even want to think about that. Let's move on.
column6: 我也希望自己永远不用顶替上位。\n那意味着瓦莱莎遭遇了可怕的事。\n我连想都不愿想。咱们换个话题吧。

column5: Oh no, I could never do that to you!\nYou need me, and all of Valinorth needs me.\nI'm not as important, but I'm still important.
column6: 哦不，我绝不会那样对你！\n你需要我，整个瓦利诺斯也需要我。\n我没那么重要，但也不是无关紧要。

column5: We're almost as important as The Elder, actually.\nHe even looks to us for guidance sometimes.\nI love the job, it just has some downsides.
column6: 其实我们几乎和长老一样重要。\n他有时甚至向我们征询意见。\n我喜欢这份工作，只是它有些短处。

column5: I wouldn't mind leaving Valinorth one day.\nBut that's probably just because I'm not allowed to.\nYou know what they say about wanting what you can't have.
column6: 有朝一日离开瓦利诺斯，我倒也不介意。\n但这大概只是因为我没被允许离开。\n你知道人们怎么说得不到的总是最好的。

column5: Yeah, it's great here!\nSometimes I wish I could leave, but it's dangerous out there.\nMazeo is the closest city, and we all know what happened there.
column6: 是啊，这儿很棒！\n有时我真希望能出去走走，可外面太危险了。\n马泽奥是最近的城，而那里出过什么事，我们都清楚。

column5: Balteus would be way too cold for me.\nAnd Alarinthia would be way too warm.\nI think we have it perfect right here.
column6: 巴尔泰乌斯对我来说太冷了。\n阿拉林西亚又太热了。\n我觉得我们这儿刚刚好。

column5: Well, it's {i}really{/i} far up north.\nThe Triumvirate is stationed there.\nI've heard their castle is amazing.
column6: 这个嘛，它在北边{i}很远{/i}的地方。\n三人执政团就驻扎在那儿。\n听说他们的城堡很壮观。

column5: But I don't think too many people live there.\nFrom what I've read, it's full of their most loyal subjects.\nSo their Honor Guard, and prospective Generals.
column6: 但我觉得住那儿的人不多。\n据我读到的，那儿全是他们最忠诚的臣民。\n比如荣誉卫队，还有未来的将军们。

column5: I've heard they have a grand library, though!\nIn Valinorth, my reading material is really limited.\nI'd say a library like that makes up for the cold.
column6: 不过我听说他们有座宏伟的图书馆！\n在瓦利诺斯，我能读的东西实在有限。\n要我说，那样的图书馆足以抵过寒冷了。

column5: The tribal lands, to the far east.\nI know very little about Alarinthia, except that it's hot.\nYou have to be really strong to live in a place like that.
column6: 那是极东之地的部族领土。\n关于阿拉林西亚我只知道那儿很热，别的几乎一无所知。\n要住在那种地方，非得特别强悍才行。

column5: And that's who lives there, mostly.\nThey take strength very seriously, and hold tournaments.\nFighting is a big deal. It determines who holds the throne.
column6: 住在那儿的主要就是这些人。\n他们极其看重力量，还举办比武大会。\n战斗可是件大事，它决定谁来坐王位。

column5: But there's barely any books on it here.\nI'm really only educated on Valinorth and Mazeo.\nMaybe someone else could teach you about Alarinthia.
column6: 可这里关于那儿的书少得可怜。\n我其实只对瓦利诺斯和马泽奥有了解。\n也许别人能给你讲讲阿拉林西亚。

column5: It's the trade hub of Alestia, full of docks and ships.\nI really hate talking about this, so I'll make it quick.\nIt's been over twenty years since The Triumvirate occupied it.
column6: 那是阿莱斯蒂亚的贸易中心，到处都是码头和船只。\n我实在讨厌谈这个，所以长话短说。\n三人执政团占领那儿已经二十多年了。

column5: They put a trade ban in effect as soon as they did.\nIt doesn't affect me too much, except for a type of apple.\nMy parents used to treat me with them when I was younger.
column6: 他们一占领就实施了贸易禁令。\n对我影响不太大，除了一种苹果。\n小时候，父母常拿那种苹果哄我。

column5: Hopefully one day they remove the stupid ban.\nThey say it keeps order on things, but I'm not sure.\nMore laws just means more rules to break, right?
column6: 但愿有一天他们会解除那条愚蠢的禁令。\n他们说这能维持秩序，可我不确定。\n法条越多，就越有规矩可以破，对吧？

column5: Anyway, yeah, Mazeo is a really interesting place.\nEveryone said the force they used to occupy it was justified.\nEliminating piracy and bringing the law to Mazeo was necessary.
column6: 总之，是啊，马泽奥是个很有意思的地方。\n大家都说他们占领时用的武力是正当的。\n为了铲除海盗、把法律带到马泽奥，那是必要的。

column5: That would be cool, but I highly doubt it.\nWe have strict orders to remain in Valinorth at all times.\nAnd Mylus isn't the type of guy to let anyone break the rules.
column6: 那会很酷，但我很怀疑。\n我们有严格的命令，必须时刻待在瓦利诺斯。\n而迈勒斯可不是那种允许任何人破例的人。

column5: It's been this way for thousands of years.\nI don't think we'll get any special treatment.\nI mean, we can dream, but it won't really go anywhere.
column6: 这规矩已经延续了几千年。\n我觉得我们不会得到什么特殊待遇。\n我是说，做梦可以，但不会有什么结果。

column5: Oh yeah? What makes you think that?\nActually, don't tell me, I don't want to get my hopes up.\nTook me long enough to come to terms with it the first time.
column6: 哦，是吗？你凭什么这么想？\n其实，别告诉我，我不想抱太大希望。\n头一回接受这事就花了我好久。

column5: It's called being a realist!\nI've come to terms with the life we have in Valinorth.\nIt took a while, but I'm sure you'll learn to do the same.
column6: 这叫务实！\n我已经接受了我们在瓦利诺斯的这种生活。\n花了一阵子，但我相信你也会慢慢接受的。

column5: This character is not in your party.
column6: 该角色不在你的队伍中。

column5: So, Valessa, do you see him anywhere?\nI don't know what he looks like, so this is on you.
column6: 那么，瓦莱莎，你看到他在哪儿了吗？\n我不知道他长什么样，所以这事就靠你了。

column5: Yeah, sorry, I'll point him out.\nI'm just not used to the villagers {i}staring{/i} like this.\nThat blade really makes us stand out, doesn't it...?
column6: 嗯，抱歉，我来指给你看。\n我只是不习惯村民们这样{i}盯着{/i}看。\n那把刀真让我们显眼，是吧……？

column5: Or maybe they're just admiring our good looks.\nCome on Valessa, don't be so uptight.\nNobody knows what this blade can do. Let 'em stare.
column6: 也许他们只是在欣赏我们的美貌呢。\n得了吧，瓦莱莎，别那么紧张。\n没人知道这把刀有什么用。让他们看呗。

column5: Wait, I see him!
column6: 等等，我看到他了！

column5: She points to a man standing near my house.{w}\nHe has his back against it, and taps his foot on the ground.{w}\nI guess he knew where I lived. Mylus must've told him.
column6: 她指着一个站在我家附近的男人。{w}\n他背靠着墙，脚尖点着地。{w}\n看来他知道我住哪儿。一定是迈勒斯告诉他的。

column5: Hey Zamira, how's your watch going?
column6: 嘿，扎米拉，你这边放哨还顺利吗？

column5: His ears perk up, and he starts to approach us.{w}\nA huge smile on his face as he quickly closes the distance.
column6: 他竖起耳朵，朝我们走来。{w}\n他脸上咧开大大的笑容，快步拉近距离。

column5: Hey Valessa! Long time no see.\nCan't complain, things are pretty much the same.\nThis is the most excitement I've had in years.
column6: 嘿，瓦莱莎！好久不见。\n没什么可抱怨的，一切照旧。\n这是我这几年遇到的最刺激的事了。

column5: He looks me up and down, before staring at the blade.{w}\nSomething told me he wouldn't stay quiet like the villagers.
column6: 他上下打量我，然后盯着那把刀。{w}\n我有种预感，他不会像村民们那样默不作声。

column5: Whoa, that thing looks pretty cool.\nI heard a few stories, but didn't get to see it.\nYou'll have to tell me more as we head to Peregrino.
column6: 哇，那玩意儿看着真酷。\n我听过一些传闻，但一直没机会见着。\n等我们去佩雷格里诺的路上，你可得跟我多讲讲。

column5: Wait, hold on! I have a few questions to ask.
column6: 等等，先别走！我有几个问题要问。

column5: Oh sure. Let's walk and talk.\nIf I'm not mistaken, we're on a schedule.
column6: 哦，当然。咱们边走边聊。\n要是我没记错，我们时间挺紧的。

column5: He points toward the gate leading out of Valinorth.\nFortaime speaks his mind as we start walking over.
column6: 他指向通往瓦利诺斯外面的那道门。\n我们开始往那边走，福泰姆说出了心里话。

column5: So you know what's coming, right?\nI just need to make sure we're on the same page.
column6: 所以你知道要发生什么，对吧？\n我只是得确认我们想法一致。

column5: Yeah. Unfortunately, I do.\nBut Mylus has a plan to keep everyone safe.\nAnd at the very least, we have a few days to prepare.
column6: 嗯。可惜，我知道。\n但迈勒斯有个保住大家安全的计划。\n至少，我们还有几天时间准备。

column5: I'm confused though. He knew about this attack.\nAnd from what he said, he's known for a while.\nWhy give up Valinorth? Why not fortify and prepare?
column6: 可我还是不明白。他早就知道这场袭击。\n而且按他说的，他知道有一阵子了。\n为什么要放弃瓦利诺斯？为什么不加固防御、做好准备？

column5: Actually, I heard something about that.\nDamek, the leader of the Rebels, had a vision.\nApparently, that blade is more than just a weapon.
column6: 其实，我听说过一些。\n反抗军的领袖达梅克看到了一个幻象。\n据说，那把刀不只是一件武器。

column5: Wait — other people can use it, then?
column6: 等等——那别人也能用它？

column5: No one else has tried, to be honest.\nBut in his vision, he saw The Triumvirate fall.\nThe cost was clear. Valinorth fell as well.
column6: 老实说，还没别人试过。\n但在他的幻象里，他看见三人执政团覆灭。\n代价很明确。瓦利诺斯也随之陷落。

column5: Who says they {i}both{/i} need to happen?\nWe could take them down without abandoning Valinorth.\nIsn't a little short-sighted to do something like that?
column6: 谁说这{i}两件事{/i}都得发生？\n我们可以在不放弃瓦利诺斯的情况下扳倒他们。\n那样做是不是有点短视了？

column5: We don't really know for sure, Valessa.\nBut it sure makes sense to replicate what he saw.\nThat way, The Rebellion's victory is guaranteed.
column6: 我们也不确定，瓦莱莎。\n但重现他所看到的，确实说得通。\n这样一来，反抗军的胜利就有了保障。

column5: Besides, Mylus will evacuate everyone that's willing.\nValinorth can be resettled in the future, I know it.\nI just worry about those who don't buy into this story.
column6: 再说，迈勒斯会疏散所有愿意走的人。\n将来瓦利诺斯还能重建，我确信。\n我只是担心那些不信这套说辞的人。

column5: What do you mean?
column6: 你什么意思？

column5: Well, some people will be stubborn.\nWe can't force them to leave. We just encourage it.\nThose that stay behind? Well, there's nothing we can do.
column6: 这个嘛，总有人会固执。\n我们不能强迫他们离开，只能劝。\n那些留下来的？唉，我们也没办法。

column5: That's true, and it lines up with the vision.\n[firstname] mentioned that lots of villagers perished.\nIsn't there something we can do to help them cooperate?
column6: 确实，这跟幻象对得上。\n[firstname]提到很多村民都死了。\n难道就没法让他们配合一下吗？

column5: That's true, and it lines up with the vision.\n[firstname] mentioned that lots of villagers perished.\nIsn't there something we can do to help them cooperate?
column6: 确实，这跟幻象对得上。\n[firstname]提到很多村民都死了。\n难道就没法让他们配合一下吗？

column5: We should focus on ourselves, Valessa.\nThere's no point wasting time on something we can't change.\nLet's get away from these prying ears. I have some more news.
column6: 我们该顾好自己，瓦莱莎。\n在我们改变不了的事上浪费时间毫无意义。\n咱们避开这些爱打听的耳朵。我还有别的消息。

column5: He smiles as we approach the exit of Valinorth.{w}\nNews? In our current situation, that doesn't sound promising.{w}\nBut with curiosity piqued, we follow Zamira with haste.
column6: 我们走近瓦利诺斯的出口时，他笑了。{w}\n消息？在如今的处境下，这听起来可不妙。{w}\n但好奇心被勾了起来，我们匆匆跟上扎米拉。

column5: You chose to play along with Damek, and convert Peregrino into a barracks.
column6: 你选择配合达梅克，把佩雷格里诺改建成兵营。

column5: You chose to keep Peregrino intact, remaining as a tavern.
column6: 你选择保留佩雷格里诺的原貌，让它继续做一间酒馆。

column5: You elected Fortaime as the Elder of Valinorth.
column6: 你推选福泰姆为瓦利诺斯的长老。

column5: You elected Valessa as the Elder of Valinorth.
column6: 你推选瓦莱莎为瓦利诺斯的长老。

column5: Taking a small detour, we decide to check out Eastcrown.{w}\nThe cold is overwhelming, so we huddle by the torchlight.
column6: 我们稍微绕了点路，决定去东冠看看。{w}\n寒冷逼人，我们挤在火把旁取暖。

column5: Oh my gosh, this is intense...!\nI've heard the stories, but I thought they were exaggerating.\nWe shouldn't stay here too long. I feel like I'm gonna die.
column6: 我的天，这也太厉害了……！\n我听过那些传闻，还以为是在夸张。\n我们不该在这儿待太久。我感觉自己要死了。

column5: Oh, Fortaime. Don't be so dramatic.\nI'm sure we have time to examine the area.\nJust don't go in any further, alright?
column6: 哦，福泰姆。别这么夸张。\n我相信我们有时间查看这片区域。\n只是别再往里走了，好吗？

column5: Yeah, I guess so. Sorry.\nLook, I can see my breath! How cool is that?
column6: 嗯，大概吧。抱歉。\n看，我能看见自己呼出的白气！多酷啊？

column5: I'll admit, that {i}is{/i} pretty cool.\nBarely out of Valinorth, and already seeing new stuff.\nI'm guessing it has something to do with the cold.
column6: 我承认，那{i}确实{/i}挺酷的。\n刚出瓦利诺斯，就见到新鲜事了。\n我猜这跟寒冷有关。

column5: It's insane...
column6: 太疯狂了……

column5: I can't believe how much the spirits help us!\nWithout their power, this is what Valinorth would look like.\nThey keep us warm, and let our village fight off the cold.
column6: 真不敢相信灵体帮了我们这么多！\n没有它们的力量，瓦利诺斯就会变成这个样子。\n它们为我们保暖，让我们的村庄抵御严寒。

column5: If Mylus is right, then this {i}is{/i} Valinorth's future.\nIt's only setting in now that I see it for myself.\nThere must be something we can do to save our village.
column6: 如果迈勒斯说得对，那这{i}就是{/i}瓦利诺斯的未来。\n亲眼所见，这感觉才刚刚沉到我心里。\n一定有什么办法能拯救我们的村庄。

column5: I sure hope so.\nLet's take a quick look around.\nIt'd be dangerous to stay here for too long.
column6: 但愿如此。\n我们快点四处看看吧。\n在这儿待太久会很危险。

column5: He inches closer to the torch, to keep himself warm.{w}\nValessa and I don't seem too bothered, and start looking around.
column6: 他一点点挪近火把，好让自己暖和点。{w}\n我和瓦莱莎好像不太受影响，开始四处查看。

column5: Valessa and Fortaime are huddled beside the torch.{w}\nTruth be told, I was cold as well. This place is intense.{w}\nI finally understand why it's remained unmapped for so long.
column6: 瓦莱莎和福泰姆挤在火把旁边。{w}\n说实话，我也冷。这地方太严酷了。{w}\n我终于明白为什么它这么久都没被测绘过。

column5: Hey, move it Valessa! You're hogging all the heat!
column6: 喂，挪挪，瓦莱莎！你把热气全霸占了！

column5: No way! Your outfit is {i}much{/i} warmer than mine!
column6: 才不！你的衣服比我{i}暖和{/i}多了！

column5: It doesn't matter! Do you want me to die or something!?
column6: 那又怎样！你想看我死吗！？

column5: Are you sure you want the answer to that question?
column6: 你确定你想知道这个问题的答案吗？

column5: What!?
column6: 什么！？

column5: They continue arguing as I walk away from the torch.{w}\nWe probably shouldn't spend too much time in Eastcrown.{w}\nWe have a long journey ahead, we can't succumb to the cold.
column6: 我离开火把时，他们还在吵。{w}\n我们大概不该在东冠待太久。{w}\n前路漫漫，我们不能被寒冷击垮。

column5: It looks like they didn't make it.
column6: 看来他们没能挺过来。

column5: I notice a book on the ground, slightly covered in snow.{w}\nI'm not sure why it's there, but I decide to take a look.{w}\nAny information about Eastcrown would be helpful to us.
column6: 我注意到地上有本书，微微覆着雪。{w}\n我不确定它为什么在那儿，但决定看看。{w}\n任何关于东冠的信息对我们都有用。

column5: Hey, are you sure you should be taking that?
column6: 嘿，你确定该拿那个吗？

column5: It was covered in snow, Fortaime.\nWhoever owned it probably forgot about it already.\nBesides, it might contain some useful information.
column6: 它都埋在雪里了，福泰姆。\n它的主人大概早把它忘了。\n再说，里面说不定有有用的信息。

column5: I guess you're right. \nBut at least put it back when you're done with it.\nI don't want to get in trouble if the owner {i}does{/i} come looking.
column6: 你说得大概没错。\n但至少看完了放回去。\n万一{i}真{/i}有主人来找，我可不想惹麻烦。

column5: Alright, you have a deal.\nSo, [firstname]; what does it say?
column6: 好，就这么定了。\n那么，[firstname]；上面写的什么？

column5: Alright, you have a deal.\nSo, [firstname]; what does it say?
column6: 好，就这么定了。\n那么，[firstname]；上面写的什么？

column5: The mountains go up so high, it's amazing.{w}\nIt's a shame that nobody will ever reach the top.{w}\nMaybe we aren't meant to find out Eastcrown's secrets.
column6: 山峰高耸入云，蔚为壮观。{w}\n可惜没人能登上峰顶。{w}\n也许我们注定无法揭开东冠的秘密。

column5: There's a flag here, but I'm not sure what it signifies.{w}\nPerhaps somebody made it that far before giving up.{w}\nI don't blame them, I'm already wanting to leave.
column6: 这里插着一面旗，但我不确定它代表什么。{w}\n也许有人走到这里就放弃了。{w}\n我不怪他们，我已经想离开了。

column5: I take a few steps down the trail, but immediately turn back.{w}\nIt actually hurts to breathe. I didn't know nature could be so hostile.{w}\nI shrug, and turn back to my friends. We may never know Eastcrown's secrets.
column6: 我沿着小径往下走了几步，立刻又折了回来。{w}\n连呼吸都疼。我没想到大自然能如此凶险。{w}\n我耸耸肩，转回朋友们身边。也许我们永远无法知晓东冠的秘密。

column5: I look off into the distance, already shivering at the extreme cold.{w}\nI wanted to visit home one time before the end, and that included Eastcrown.{w}\nWe never got to find out what was out there. I start to wonder if we ever will.
column6: 我眺望远方，极寒已让我瑟瑟发抖。{w}\n我本想在这结束前回一次家，其中就包括东冠。{w}\n我们始终没能查明那里有什么。我开始怀疑，我们是否还能有机会。

column5: Not that it's even important.{w}\nIt has nothing to do with our goal, or our cause.{w}\nIt's just a mystery — one of many left unsolved.
column6: 倒不是说这有多重要。{w}\n它跟我们的目标、我们的事业毫无关系。{w}\n它只是个谜——众多未解之谜中的一个。

column5: Howl approaches me from behind, and looks into Eastcrown.{w}\nHe seems perplexed, like not even he really knows what's over there.{w}\nIt makes sense. I doubt The Old Monarchy had the ability to survive the cold.
column6: 豪尔从身后走近我，望向东冠。{w}\n他似乎很困惑，好像连他也不清楚那边有什么。{w}\n这说得通。我怀疑旧王朝没有能力在这严寒中存活。

column5: We know this place.
column6: 我们知道这地方。

column5: He holds out his hand, feeling the harsh winds.
column6: 他伸出手，感受凛冽的寒风。

column5: The fatal cold — death within an hour.\nNo chance of survival. Not like Alarinthia's deserts.\nWe let criminals handle their own end. A mercy.
column6: 致命的严寒——一小时内便丧命。\n毫无生还可能。跟阿拉林西亚的沙漠不一样。\n我们让罪犯自行了断。是一种恩慈。

column5: Because of this, it became a very mysterious place.\nWe started to wonder what was out there — if anything.\nHowever, until now, we had no way of finding out. Hmm.
column6: 正因如此，它成了一个非常神秘的地方。\n我们开始好奇那边有什么——如果有的话。\n然而直到现在，我们都无从得知。唔。

column5: Until now...?
column6: 直到现在……？

column5: This cold. We feel nothing.\nIt wouldn't harm us to venture forward.\nPerhaps now is the time to solve this mystery.
column6: 这种寒冷。我们毫无感觉。\n往前探一探对我们并无大碍。\n也许现在是解开这个谜团的时候了。

column5: How fitting that we would be the first.\nA monument to death. An execution ground.\nMonarch. We would like to take a brief break.
column6: 由我们来做第一个，再合适不过。\n一座死亡的纪念碑。一片刑场。\n君主。我们想稍作休息。

column5: How does he know for sure that he can survive...?{w}\nHe may not feel anything, but the body could still freeze.
column6: 他怎么能确定自己一定能活下来……？{w}\n他也许感觉不到什么，但身体照样会冻僵。

column5: Unlikely. We would be shielded by our spirits.\nThey may die, one by one, but we would endure.\nAt the end of it, we would remain largely unchanged.
column6: 不太可能。我们的灵体护卫着我们。\n它们也许会一个接一个地消亡，但我们会撑住。\n到最后，我们大体上仍会保持不变。

column5: Besides, we were not asking for permission.\nDo you not share the same curiosity as us...?
column6: 再说，我们并不是在征求许可。\n你难道没有和我们一样的好奇心吗……？

column5: Interesting. Perhaps you are better than us.\nWe are not surprised, given the role you play.\nIf there is anything of note, however, we will tell.
column6: 有意思。也许你比我们更强。\n考虑到你扮演的角色，我们并不意外。\n不过，若有什么值得注意的，我们会告诉你。

column5: We thought so, too. Something about great minds.\nPerhaps there will be nothing. Or perhaps not.\nIt is something we will never know until we try.
column6: 我们也这么想。所谓英雄所见略同。\n也许什么都没有。也许不然。\n这事不试就永远不会知道。

column5: He takes a few steps forward, and looks down at the ground.
column6: 他向前走了几步，低头看着地面。

column5: Already, we can feel our power dwindling.\nThe spirits inside come forth to keep us warm.\nWe will hurry, and return with minimal damage.
column6: 我们已经能感觉到力量在衰减。\n体内的灵体涌出来为我们保暖。\n我们会快点，尽量少受损伤地回来。

column5: He starts walking away, powered by his curiosity.{w}\nI guess he couldn't resist solving a mystery of the world.{w}\nI don't blame him. He was also uniquely qualified to do so.
column6: 他凭着好奇心，迈步走远。{w}\n我想他就是忍不住要去解开世界的一个谜团。{w}\n我不怪他。而且他也确实有独一无二的资格这么做。

column5: There must be something important inside Eastcrown.{w}\nIt was too mysterious. There had to be something there.{w}\nAnd now, we'd finally find that out. It was rather exciting.
column6: 东冠之内一定有什么重要的东西。{w}\n它太神秘了。那里一定藏着什么。{w}\n而现在，我们终于要弄清楚了。真让人兴奋。

column5: There was probably nothing of note in Eastcrown.{w}\nIt was mysterious because we made it that way.{w}\nIt's nothing. Just the top of a mountain.
column6: 东冠里大概没什么值得注意的东西。{w}\n它之所以神秘，是因为我们自己把它想得神秘。{w}\n没什么。不过是一座山的山顶。

column5: I hold those thoughts in my mind until Howl returns.{w}\nHe shows no signs of wear, and walks as strong as ever.{w}\nIt's hard to get a read on his face. There's no emotion on display.
column6: 我抱着这些念头，直到豪尔回来。{w}\n他看不出一点疲态，步伐一如既往地稳健。{w}\n他的表情很难读懂。脸上不显任何情绪。

column5: We don't understand.\nFor a while, there was nothing.\nBut then — we saw something interesting.
column6: 我们不明白。\n有好一阵子，什么都没有。\n可后来——我们看到了点有意思的东西。

column5: I ask him to elaborate — my curiosity taking control.
column6: 我让他说详细点——好奇心主宰了我。

column5: Eastcrown is ice. There's no water anywhere.\nIt doesn't make any sense. We saw a ship.\nCrashed, broken. Frozen among the ice.
column6: 东冠全是冰。哪儿都没有水。\n这说不通。我们看见了一艘船。\n撞毁了，破碎了。冻结在冰层之中。

column5: A ship — sailing in ice. This is backwards.\nBut we think that perhaps this is okay.\nBackwards. Just like our thoughts.
column6: 一艘船——在冰上航行。这是反过来的。\n但我们觉得，也许这没什么。\n反过来。就像我们的思维一样。

column5: Now he's lost me...
column6: 这下我听不明白了……

column5: The future...? Or perhaps the past.\nThis new outlook changes almost everything.\nDo not worry, [firstname]. We were harmed in no way.
column6: 未来……？又或者是过去。\n这个新视角几乎改变了一切。\n别担心，[firstname]。我们没有受到任何伤害。

column5: As we said, the spirits inside kept us warm.\nA self-sacrifice that helped us brave the cold. A noble end.\nWe are lesser now, but only slightly; and it is an interesting feeling.
column6: 如我们所说，体内的灵体为我们保暖。\n这是帮我们抵御严寒的自我牺牲。一种高贵的终结。\n我们现在虚弱了些，但只是略微；这感觉挺有意思。

column5: What we saw in Eastcrown is of no real importance.\nHowever, it has conjured up a spark in our minds.\nA spark that we must discuss promptly in Mazeo.
column6: 我们在东冠看到的东西其实无关紧要。\n不过，它在我们的脑海中激起了一点火花。\n这火花，我们必须尽快到马泽奥去商议。

column5: There are some final matters to take care of before the end.\nThank you for coming here, [firstname]. If anything, it benefits us.\nI'm sorry if this wasn't what you expected. But that's not always a bad thing.
column6: 在结束之前，还有些最后的事要处理。\n谢谢你来到这里，[firstname]。无论如何，这对我们有好处。\n要是这不符你的期望，我很抱歉。但那也不总是坏事。

column5: I nod. As long as he found some sort of benefit in his little trip.{w}\nBefore our final battle, everybody needed to be committed to the cause.{w}\nOne error, one slip-up could cost all of us our lives. We had to be resolute.
column6: 我点点头。只要他这趟小出行有所收获就好。{w}\n在最终之战前，每个人都必须全心投入这项事业。{w}\n一个失误、一次疏忽，都可能让我们所有人丧命。我们必须坚定。

column5: But I wonder what he could want to talk about so suddenly.{w}\nThe future? Thinking backwards? Something was definitely bothering him.{w}\nI'd have to do my duty as his leader to quell any worry before we launch our attack.
column6: 但我好奇，他突然想谈什么。{w}\n未来？反向思考？他心里一定有什么事困扰着。{w}\n身为他的领袖，我得尽本分，在发起进攻前消除一切顾虑。

column5: Howl's loyalty scene is now available at the War Table in Mazeo.{w}\nClick his icon in order to access this scene and earn his loyalty.
column6: 豪尔的忠诚剧情现已在马泽奥的作战桌解锁。{w}\n点击他的图标即可进入该剧情，赢得他的忠诚。

column5: It looks like something is bothering Fortaime.{w}\nI approach him, and decide to ask what's on his mind.{w}\nHe seems a little startled, like he was indeed lost in thought.
column6: 看来福泰姆有心事。{w}\n我走近他，决定问问他心里在想什么。{w}\n他似乎有点受惊，像是确实陷入了沉思。

column5: Oh, hey there [firstname].\nWhat's wrong...? Nothing, really.\nI'm just thinking about, well, everything.
column6: 哦，你好啊，[firstname]。\n怎么了……？没什么，真的。\n我只是在想，呃，一切。

column5: Oh, hey there [firstname].\nWhat's wrong...? Nothing, really.\nI'm just thinking about, well, everything.
column6: 哦，你好啊，[firstname]。\n怎么了……？没什么，真的。\n我只是在想，呃，一切。

column5: This will be the last time we see Peregrino.\nWhen and if we come back, it'll be a barracks.\nI know that's what I wanted, but I had fun here.
column6: 这将是我们最后一次看到佩雷格里诺。\n等我们回来时，它会变成兵营。\n我知道这是我想要的，但我在这儿过得很开心。

column5: I'm just thinking about the future a lot...
column6: 我只是思虑未来想得太多了……

column5: I got a good sleep last night, so that helped.\nBetter than being restless and alone with my thoughts.\nI'm just thinking about the future a lot right now.
column6: 我昨晚睡了个好觉，所以好多了。\n总比辗转反侧、独自胡思乱想强。\n我现在只是思虑未来想得太多了。

column5: I gotta figure out how to make you proud. As Elder, I mean.\nJust give me some time to figure stuff out — then I'll shine.\nIt's not like I can fully adapt to being our leader in one night.
column6: 我得想办法让你为我骄傲。我是说，作为长老。\n给我点时间理清头绪——然后我就会大放异彩。\n我总不能一夜之间就完全适应当我们的领袖。

column5: Most importantly, it's Valinorth's future that concerns me.\nWe know what Valessa wants to do as Elder, but I'm worried.\nI've read that nations fall due to a leader's stubborn nature.
column6: 最重要的是，我担心的是瓦利诺斯的未来。\n我们知道瓦莱莎当长老后想怎么做，可我很担心。\n我读到过，国家会因领袖的固执而衰亡。

column5: I'd rather see Valinorth live alongside the other nations.\nIt's a lot preferable to the concept of dying alone.\nI think it's just time to turn some pages, you know?
column6: 我更希望看到瓦利诺斯与其他国家共存。\n这比独自消亡的结局强多了。\n我觉得是时候翻篇了，你懂吗？

column5: He gives me a nervous laugh, before shuffling awkwardly.{w}\nThere's something else on his mind. I can tell.{w}\nBut it's not my place to pry, so I wait for him to speak.
column6: 他冲我紧张地笑了笑，然后局促地挪了挪身子。{w}\n他还有别的心事。我看得出来。{w}\n但轮不到我刨根问底，于是我等着他开口。

column5: Thanks for letting me sleep here with you, by the way.\nIt helped me process things in my head a little bit more.\nIf it weren't for that, I would've been too scared to think.
column6: 对了，谢谢你让我在这儿跟你一起睡。\n这帮我多梳理了一下脑子里的事。\n要不是这样，我早就吓得没法思考了。

column5: Like — what if they attacked in the middle of the night?\nWe all know they'd have to pass by Peregrino first.\nI was honestly scared we might die here last night.
column6: 比如——要是他们半夜来袭怎么办？\n我们都知道他们得先经过佩雷格里诺。\n老实说，昨晚我真怕我们会死在这儿。

column5: So yeah — thanks a million.\nBut there's one more thing I want to say.\nLast night, I had a really bad dream...
column6: 所以——太谢谢你了。\n不过还有件事我想说。\n昨晚，我做了个很可怕的梦……

column5: I know I look pretty well rested, but I'm not.\nThis is pretty embarrassing for me to say, so don't laugh.\nLast night — I had a really bad dream. I almost cried.
column6: 我知道我看起来休息得不错，其实没有。\n说这话挺让我难为情的，别笑。\n昨晚——我做了个很可怕的梦。我差点哭出来。

column5: We were making our way down toward Mazeo.\nBut we weren't with Pro and Ulric. It was our parents.\nI kept telling them not to go. I knew they wouldn't come back.
column6: 我们正朝着马泽奥的方向走。\n但同行的人不是普洛和乌尔里克。而是我们的父母。\n我一直叫他们别去。我知道他们不会回来了。

column5: He clenches his fists, and trembles slightly.
column6: 他攥紧拳头，微微颤抖。

column5: But they didn't listen. They just kept going.\nI ran until my legs could barely move. Then I ran even more.\nIt actually felt like I could save them, if I only tried.
column6: 可他们不听。他们就那样一路往前走。\n我跑到双腿几乎动弹不得。然后又接着跑。\n那种感觉就像是，只要我肯努力，就真能救下他们。

column5: Eventually, we made it to the gates of Mazeo.\nOr at least I think they were. I've never actually been there.\nBut this is the worst part. They finally turned to face us.
column6: 最后，我们到了马泽奥的城门前。\n至少我觉得那是城门。我从没真正去过那儿。\n但这还不是最糟的。他们终于转过身来面对我们。

column5: And that's when I realized something shocking...\nI don't remember what my parents look like, [firstname].\nTheir faces were a blur, almost like they were nobody.
column6: 就在那时，我意识到一件令人震惊的事……\n我不记得我父母长什么样了，[firstname]。\n他们的脸一片模糊，简直就像无名之辈。

column5: And that's when I realized something shocking...\nI don't remember what my parents look like, [firstname].\nTheir faces were a blur, almost like they were nobody.
column6: 就在那时，我意识到一件令人震惊的事……\n我不记得我父母长什么样了，[firstname]。\n他们的脸一片模糊，简直就像无名之辈。

column5: They started to speak, but I didn't recognize their voices.\nHas it been so long that I'm forgetting my own parents...?\nI tried so hard to picture them when I woke up. I couldn't.
column6: 他们开口说话，可我认不出他们的声音。\n是过了太久，我连自己的父母都要忘了吗……？\n醒来后我拼命想回忆起他们的模样。却怎么也做不到。

column5: When they died, everyone told me they weren't really gone.\nThat they'd live on forever — inside of my memory.\nBut even that's fading, [firstname]. What happens next...?
column6: 他们去世时，所有人都说他们并没有真正离开。\n说他们会永远活着——活在我的记忆里。\n可连那也在消退，[firstname]。接下来又会怎样……？

column5: Back at the Grand Tree, we shared a common goal.\nWe wanted to fight The Triumvirate to avenge our parents.\nBut this dream was sort of a wake up call, you know...?
column6: 在巨树那儿时，我们有个共同的目标。\n我们想对抗三人执政团，为父母报仇。\n但这个梦有点像一记当头棒喝，你懂吗……？

column5: Back at the Grand Tree, I said I wanted vengeance.\nI wanted to take down The Triumvirate to avenge our parents.\nBut this dream was kind of like a wake up call, you know...?
column6: 在巨树那儿时，我说我想要复仇。\n我想打倒三人执政团，为父母报仇。\n但这个梦有点像一记当头棒喝，你懂吗……？

column5: Why should I fight for something that doesn't exist?\nAnd better yet — something I can't even picture in my head.\nThere are so many reasons to fight, all of them less selfish.
column6: 我为什么要为一个并不存在的东西而战？\n更不用说——一个我连想都想象不出来的东西。\n战斗的理由多得是，每一个都没那么自私。

column5: So I think I want to fight for {i}you{/i}.\nI want to make sure that you're safe, and you survive this.\nWhen it comes to you, the entirety of Alestia is at stake.
column6: 所以我想，我要为{i}你{/i}而战。\n我要确保你平安，确保你挺过这一切。\n涉及到你，整个阿莱斯蒂亚都攸关安危。

column5: He continues to tremble, and I can tell he's fighting back tears.{w}\nIt's almost like this dream is helping him move on from his parents.{w}\nHe's becoming more grounded in reality — in the here and now.
column6: 他仍在颤抖，我看得出他在强忍泪水。{w}\n这个梦几乎像是在帮他走出父母离世的阴影。{w}\n他正变得越发脚踏实地——活在此时此刻。

column5: I take a few steps forward, and wrap my arms around him.{w}\nHe gasps in surprise, and I notice his trembling come to a halt.{w}\nA few moments later, I feel his arms return the hug, squeezing tight.
column6: 我向前走几步，张开双臂抱住他。{w}\n他惊讶地吸了口气，我注意到他的颤抖停了下来。{w}\n片刻之后，我感觉到他的手臂回抱住我，紧紧收紧。

column5: I just miss them so much...
column6: 我只是太想他们了……
